items.title: El papa León se someterá a una cirugía para extirpar un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo.
items.body:
El papa León dijo el domingo que los médicos le habían detectado un pequeño nódulo en el pulmón durante un chequeo médico y que se sometería a una intervención quirúrgica esta semana para extirparlo, en lo que supone el primer episodio de preocupación relacionado con su salud desde que ocupa el cargo.
León, de 71 años, explicó a los peregrinos reunidos en la Plaza de San Pedro para su oración dominical semanal que el nódulo estaba "bien localizado" y se había detectado a tiempo, y les pidió que oraran "por la visita pastoral que voy a realizar" a Uruguay, Argentina y Perú.
"Recientemente, durante unos exámenes médicos, los médicos encontraron un nódulo localizado en mi pulmón", dijo el pontífice. "Se detectó en una fase muy temprana y está bien localizado".
"Los médicos consideran aconsejable intervenir, por lo que, siguiendo su consejo, he decidido someterme a una intervención quirúrgica para extirparlo", añadió. "La operación ya está programada para los próximos días".
Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. Según la Sociedad Torácica Americana, menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores.
Leo, elegido papa por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es más joven de lo usual para ser jefe de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, entre ellos el tenis, y no se tiene constancia de que haya tenido problemas de salud antes.
Su predecesor, el difunto papa Francisco, falleció a los 88 años y se encontraba cada vez más débil en sus últimos años.
La oficina de prensa del Vaticano indicó que se esperaba que la recuperación de Leo tras la intervención quirúrgica durara aproximadamente una semana. No facilitó de inmediato más detalles sobre el estado de salud del papa.
Leo tiene una agenda muy apretada y tiene previsto realizar una gira de 11 días por Uruguay, Argentina y Perú del 6 al 17 de noviembre.

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo said on Sunday (Oct 11) that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
Pope Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.
The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant.
"Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localised nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."

"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days."
A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5 per cent of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size and other factors such as smoking.
Pope Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.

Related:

Pope Leo warns that AI is creating 'paradise of machines'

Pope Leo urges concessions for peace as Ukraine war drags on

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well.
"I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement.
"The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it during today’s Angelus are reassuring," Meloni added.
The late Pope Francis, Pope Leo's predecessor, died at age 88 and was increasingly frail in his later years.
The Vatican press office said the pope's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health.
Pope Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17.
Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake".

Source: Reuters/fh

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[バチカン市国 １１日 ロイター] - ローマ教皇レオ１４世（７１）は１２日、先の健康診断で肺に小さなしこりが見つかり、今週中に切除手術を受けると明らかにした。２０２５年５月の就任後、健康問題が明らかになるのは初めて。

バチカンのサンピエトロ広場で行った日曜恒例の祈りの集いで信者らに説明した。しこりは局所的なもので、ごく早期に発見されたという。

教皇は「（医師の）助言に従い、切除手術を受けることを決めた」と述べた。手術は数日以内に予定されているという。

レオ１４世は７１歳と教皇としては比較的若く、テニスなどのスポーツを好む。これまで大きな健康問題は知られていなかった。前任のフランシスコ教皇は晩年、健康状態が悪化し、８８歳で死去した。

バチカン報道官室によると、レオ１４世は術後１週間程度で回復する見通し。健康状態について、それ以上の詳細は明らかにしていない。

items.body:
Cricket-India hold off West Indies to take 2-1 series lead in third T20
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 23:21 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 23:21 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

India beat West Indies by 14 runs on Sunday in Indore to take a 2-1 lead in the five-match Twenty20 International series. Chasing 224 for victory, West Indies suffered an early setback when Arshdeep Singh dismissed captain Shai Hope for five after he missed a swipe at a delivery that jagged back on to his stumps.
Shimron Hetmyer kept the visitors in the hunt with a brisk 43 off 26 balls before spinner Naman Dhir broke the stand, while Axar Patel removed Rovman Powell to leave West Indies struggling to match the mounting required rate. Quentin Sampson and Sherfane Rutherford briefly revived the chase, but West Indies could not sustain the momentum as wickets fell regularly in the closing overs and they finished on 209-7.
Arshdeep was India's standout bowler with 3-44 as the hosts defended a formidable 223 after being asked to bat. India recovered from the early loss of Sanju Samson, who fell for just three to Shamar Joseph, through a 108-run partnership for the second wicket between Abhishek Sharma and Ishan Kishan.
Sharma dominated the scoring with an explosive 69 off 30 balls, while Kishan contributed 37. However, the hosts lost momentum when Kishan's dismissal triggered a middle-order collapse. The platform laid by Sharma ultimately proved decisive, allowing the lower order to keep the scoreboard moving and lift India to 223 before they were bowled out off the final delivery of the innings.
The teams meet again in the fourth Twenty20 International in Hyderabad on Wednesday.

Saudi Arabia reports injuries in new attack at Riyadh airport, day after strike kills 13
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 23:19 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 23:19 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed responsibility for Saturday's strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, as Saudi authorities reported people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday. The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. An unspecified number of people were injured, the Saudi civil aviation authority said, adding it was still assessing the damage.
The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport. The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war in Yemen by the Yemeni government against the Iran-aligned group.
The airport has been closed since Saturday's attack. However, a long-planned international energy conference went ahead in Riyadh on Sunday as planned. HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS
In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and also said the group had attacked the airport in Dammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. Reuters has reached out to the Saudi media office and to Aramco for comment.
The Houthis earlier on Sunday had renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers, and travellers against using Saudi airports. "We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said.
'WORSE IS YET TO COME,' HOUTHIS WARN Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours, including the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada. Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.
"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television. US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD The five-day conference of international energy organizations WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport.
Meanwhile, a ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available and it was not clear which ministers joined the meeting. Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting the event, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link.
German officials were trying to organise a return flight for Economy Minister Katherina Reiche, who was in Riyadh to attend the WPC conference and ministers' meeting. She was supposed to return to Berlin on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely that her flight would not be able to take off due to the closure of the airport and alternatives were being considered.
Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes at all schools in Riyadh would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff. In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said. India's embassy in Riyadh said on Sunday one of its citizens injured in the attack had died, adding to the initial death toll of 12.
Four people were killed in the two previous attacks on the airport earlier in the week. One of the attacks also caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

The US is threatening to stop the procurement system that provides Ukraine with weapons in order to press Kyiv to halt its deep strikes on Russian energy infrastructure, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing officials in Europe.
The officials, who received calls from US officials or were briefed on them, said that the US was lobbying European capitals and Kyiv to try to end the attacks on Russian oil refineries, the report added. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The message from the US included threats to cut off intelligence sharing and Purl (the Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List) mechanism for procuring US weapons for Ukraine, the report added. "They are calling Kyiv . ... They are calling everyone [in Europe]," said an official who received a call from a US defence official, as per the report.
The report comes after US President Donald Trump made a surprise announcement on Sunday of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine that he said was "effective immediately," but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal. "Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote.

items.title: Pope Leo says he will undergo surgery for small growth on lung
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
items.body:
Pope Leo said on Sunday that doctors had detected a small growth on his lung during a recent health check and he would be undergoing surgery this week to remove it, in the first health scare of the 71-year-old pontiff's tenure.
Leo told pilgrims in St. Peter's Square for his weekly Sunday prayer that the growth, a small nodule, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early.
The Vatican did not say whether the nodule is believed to be malignant.
"Recently, during some medical examinations, doctors found a localized nodule in my lung," said the pontiff. "It was detected at a very early stage and is well contained."
"The doctors believe it is advisable to intervene, so, following their advice, I have decided to undergo surgery to remove it," he said. "The operation is already scheduled for the next few days."
A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.
"Lung nodules are fairly common and are often benign," said Stephen Liu, a lung cancer expert at Georgetown University in Washington and division chief of hematology-oncology at MedStar Georgetown University Hospital.
"When there is sufficient concern, and when it is safe to do so, based on the location of the nodule and the overall health of the patient, surgical removal can provide a definitive diagnosis," he said.
LEO A RELATIVELY YOUNG POPE, PLAYS SPORTS Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to previously have had health issues.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni wished the pope well.
"I would like to express to the Holy Father my personal support, and that of the Italian government, as he faces this challenge in the coming days," she said in a statement.
"The serenity and composure with which he spoke about it (today) ...are reassuring," Meloni added.
The late Pope Francis, Leo's predecessor, died at age 88. He was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years. He did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health.
The Vatican press office said Leo's recovery from surgery was expected to take about a week. It did not immediately provide further details about the pope's health.
Leo keeps a busy schedule and is due to make an 11-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6-17.
Before mentioning his health issue in his address on Sunday, the pope referred to the trip, thanking Catholics for their prayers "for the pastoral visit I will undertake."

Mexico's Sheinbaum urges coastal residents to remain indoors as Hurricane Simon nears coast
Reuters | Updated: 11-10-2026 23:08 IST | Created: 11-10-2026 23:08 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

MEXICO CITY, Oct 11 - Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents along the country's Pacific coast to remain indoors on Sunday as powerful Category 4 Hurricane Simon approached Mexico's west-central coast, threatening destructive winds, dangerous storm surges and potentially deadly flooding. Simon was located about 65 miles (105 km) west-northwest of the port city of Manzanillo, in Colima state, with maximum sustained winds of 145 mph (230 kph), the US National Hurricane Center (NHC) said in its latest advisory at 9 a.m. local time.
The hurricane was moving north-northwest at 11 kph (7 mph), with its center about 140 km (85 miles) south-southeast of Cabo Corrientes, in neighboring Jalisco state. "With the approaching impact of Category 4 Hurricane Simon, we urge residents of coastal municipalities in Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacan to remain sheltered until authorities officially declare that the danger has passed," Sheinbaum said in a post on X.
She said precautionary evacuations to safer areas were continuing and urged residents to stay off the streets and follow civil protection instructions. The NHC said Simon was expected to move very near Mexico's west-central coast later on Sunday and remain close to the coast on Monday, although forecast uncertainty remained over whether the center would cross inland or remain just offshore.
Even without a direct landfall, dangerous storm surges, large destructive waves and damaging winds were likely along portions of Mexico's west-central coast, the forecaster warned. Mexico's National Civil Protection Coordination (CNPC) placed 28 municipalities in Jalisco and Colima under its highest cyclone alert level, while another 93 municipalities were under a high alert level, according to civil protection bulletins.
Puerto Vallarta's international airport has temporarily closed, while authorities have suspended nonessential activities and opened emergency shelters in threatened coastal communities. The NHC warned that heavy rainfall through Monday could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, particularly in mountainous areas.
Simon intensified rapidly into a Category 4 hurricane on Saturday, prompting authorities to deploy military personnel, emergency workers and civil protection teams to vulnerable coastal communities. The storm comes a week after Hurricane Polo struck Mexico's Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 hurricane, toppling trees and utility poles and flooding streets.

By Gopal Sharma
KATHMANDU, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.

Two women and three men were out of contact, the national disaster authority said. The army said a further 49 people, including a foreigner, had been rescued. They did not give the person’s nationality.

A landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said.

Show Full Article

The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.

“We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe,” said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district’s most senior bureaucrat.

The flood swept away about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.

The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.

National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood.

“Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed,” the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post.

Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

(Reporting by Gopal Sharma; Editing by Jamie Freed and Kate Mayberry)

WARSAW, Oct 11 (Reuters) – Polish security services convened a special meeting on Sunday after receiving information about a potential attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz, an Interior Ministry spokesperson said on X.

The exact nature of the threat and its origin were not immediately clear.

“Following information received by the Polish Police regarding a possible attack …Interior Minister, Marcin Kierwiński, and the Minister-Coordinator of Special Services, Tomasz Siemoniak, have ordered action to be taken in this matter,” spokesperson Karolina Galecka wrote.

Show Full Article

“A meeting will be held today at 11:00 a.m. at the Internal Security Agency’s Counter-Terrorism Centre.”

A spokesperson for the minister-coordinator of special services said he had no further comment.

Private broadcaster Radio Zet reported that police had received an email with information about the threat.

While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.

In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of calling for the assassination of senior Polish politicians.

In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an assassination attempt on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

Sunday’s announcement came as authorities in Poland have been on high alert following a wave of violence in schools that resulted in the death of a caretaker on Thursday.

(Reporting by Alan CharlishEditing by Tomasz Janowski and Christina Fincher)

items.title: サウジ首都空港に飛翔体、フーシ派「作戦区域」と主張　10日の攻撃認める
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Jana Choukeir　Maha El Dahan　Timour Azhari

［ドバイ／リヤド　１１日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Jana Choukeir　Maha El Dahan　Timour Azhari

［ドバイ／リヤド　１１日　ロイター］ - イエメンで軍事作戦を行っているサウジアラビア主導の連合軍は１１日、首都リヤドのキング・ハーリド国際空港に「正体不明の飛翔体」が飛来し、火災が発生したと発表した。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派は、死傷者が多数出た１０日の同空港への攻撃を認めた。

連合軍は、飛翔体は同空港の第４ターミナルを狙ったもので、同空港付近で迎撃したとしている。空港は１０日の攻撃で閉鎖されている。 

フーシ派は１１日、航空会社や旅行者、空港関係者に対し、サウジアラビア国内の空港に近づかないよう警告していた。Ｘへの投稿で「全ての航空会社、専門家、従業員、労働者、旅行者に対し、サウジの空港と領空を使用しないよう改めて警告する。（聖地である）メッカとメディナの空港を除き、サウジの空港と領空は攻撃に対して脆弱（ぜいじゃく）であり、われわれの作戦部隊の作戦区域となっている」と表明。「迎撃に失敗した場合の責任はサウジ側にある」とした。またフーシ派の「外務省」は「サウジという敵がイエメンへの侵略と干渉をやめなければ、さらに悪い事態が訪れるだろう」と述べた。フーシ派系メディアが伝えた。

キング・ハーリド国際空港への１０日の攻撃では、少なくとも１２人が死亡し、３００人余りが負傷した。サウジ当局によると、死者は、サウジ人が４人、バングラデシュ人２人のほか、米国、ヨルダン、パレスチナ、シリア、スーダン、エジプト国籍の人が含まれる。トランプ米大統領は、サウジの対フーシ派軍事作戦に参加するか「検討」する考えを示した。

サウジ主導の連合軍は１０日、サウジ東部ダンマームのキング・ファハド国際空港付近にも飛翔体が落下したと発表した。

フーシ派は１１日、ダンマームの空港とアラムコ施設を攻撃したと表明した。

サウジのエネルギー省は、１１─１５日の日程でリヤドで開催する世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は予定通り実施すると発表した。

items.title: HSBC leads international banks in financing India Inc across debt, equity
items.author: Subrata Panda
items.summary: The bank topped G3 bonds and syndicated loans, and ranked among the leading international investment banks for equity fundraising ...
items.body: London-headquartered HSBC in January-September 2026 was the leading international bank in facilitating fundraising by Indian companies through bonds issued in major international currencies, syndicated loans, and initial public offerings (IPOs), according to Hitendra Dave, chief executive officer (CEO) of the lender’s India unit. This has been done by leveraging the bank’s corporate and institutional relations and its ability to connect borrowers with pools of capital seeking to invest in debt and equity opportunities in India. The bank moved up from third place in G3 bonds (bonds issued in euros, dollars, or the yen) last year, retained its lead in syndicated loans for a third consecutive year, and ranked second among international investment banks for primary equity fundraising through IPOs and qualified institutional placements (QIPs) since January 2025. In IPOs alone (year-to-date), it is the leading international bank to facilitate primary fundraise. “Our financing business spans three markets: Loans, bonds and equity, including IPOs and QIPs… (We have done) financing for companies making overseas acquisitions, funding capex, refinancing or retiring rupee loans, and meeting other funding needs. We also hold the largest market share in G3 bonds, based on volumes raised by local banks. In equity, we are number one in IPOs and number two in QIPs,” Dave told Business Standard. HSBC was also among the leading banks in mobilising deposits under the Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) scheme, raising $14.5 billion between June and August. It ranked second to ICICI Bank, which rang up nearly $18 billion. Banks collectively raised nearly $133 billion under this facility. Dave attributed HSBC’s mobilisation to its strong non-resident Indian (NRI) franchise and presence across global markets. “I don’t want HSBC to be strong only in financing. We want to build the business in a way that puts us ahead of the competition. In areas such as wealth, local banks are doing better than us. But our ambition is to be number one or number two in every segment we operate in, and at least in the top three where that isn’t possible,” Dave said. HSBC’s debt-market performance was reflected in its transaction mandates. According to the Bloomberg data, the bank topped India’s G3 bond-league table in January-September 2026, moving up from third place last year. It also ranked as the leading bookrunner for syndicated loans originating in India for a third consecutive year, with a 21 per cent share in volumes, according to Dealogic. In the G3 bond market, HSBC worked on a $1 billion dual-tranche offer by Export-Import Bank of India, a $750 million bond sale by the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID), and a $1 billion issue by ICICI Bank. Its other mandates included a $700 million offer by Bank of Baroda and a $600 million bond sale by renewable energy company ReNew Power. India’s G3 bond issuance reached $21.8 billion by late September. This is nearly four times the $5.54 billion raised in all of 2025 and is approaching the previous annual record of about $22.4 billion. In syndicated lending, HSBC solely arranged $100 million rupee-denominated acquisition financing for Waaree RTL, following the Reserve Bank of India’s liberalisation of onshore acquisition-financing regulations. Other mandates included a $125 million debut syndicated loan for RateGain to support a cross-border strategic acquisition and an $85 million, seven-year syndicated term loan for Piramal Pharma to finance cross-border capital expenditure, with repayments aligned to projected cash flows. The bank also arranged $1 billion in financing for A. V. Minerals (Novelis) for its cross-border funding and secured mandates for $450 million across three transactions for Bank of Maharashtra. HSBC attributed its position in syndicated lending to its first-mover advantage in novel financing structures and its status as a preferred lender for large Indian companies undertaking acquisitions. In equity capital, HSBC completed six IPOs worth about $5 billion in January-September 2026 and led four of the five largest ones during the period, accounting for 84 per cent of their combined deal value, according to the bank. It was present in the three largest IPOs identified by HSBC: Jio Platforms’ $4 billion (which is coming), the National Stock Exchange’s $2.4 billion, and SBI Funds Management’s $1.3 billion. HSBC said it was leading eight of the 12 largest forthcoming IPOs, including those of Avaada Electro, Zetwerk and AGS Eye, apart from the one of Jio Platforms. Additionally, the bank facilitated fundraising by Indian companies through QIPs, including State Bank of India’s $2.9 billion, JSW Infrastructure’s $794 million, and Biocon’s $460 million.

items.title: At least 139 migrants dead, including some children, after boat from Djibouti to Yemen capsizes, UN agency says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
items.body:
At least 139 migrants, including at least 15 children, have died and around 84 are missing after a boat carrying more than 300 people capsized while sailing from Djibouti to Yemen, the United Nations' International Organization for Migration said on Sunday.
The boat, carrying 305 people, capsized near Guhere, north of Obock — a port town in Djibouti — during the night of October 8-9, the IOM said, citing survivor accounts.
Around 82 people survived the shipwreck, the statement said. A spokesperson for the Ethiopian government did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Photographs shared by the UN agency showed worn-out sandals and sneakers washed up on the shore.
"Our teams are on the ground alongside local authorities to provide emergency assistance," said IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti Alexandre Coissac.
"This tragedy is a stark reminder of the dangers faced by migrants along this migration corridor as they seek economic opportunities," Coissac said.
Djiboutian authorities are continuing search and rescue operations, the IOM statement said, adding that local authorities are also providing medical care to survivors and arranging burials for the deceased.
The Djibouti government could not be immediately reached for comment.
The migrants were heading to Yemen, with the hope of eventually making it to wealthier Gulf nations, even as Yemeni nationals themselves [USN:L6N45E0CP TEXT:"flee their country"], which is [USN:L6N45T0PU TEXT:"experiencing"] the most serious escalation in fighting between Saudi Arabia-backed government forces and the Iran-backed Houthis since a UN-brokered truce in 2022.
"Despite the violence in Yemen, migrants are still making the perilous journeys hoping to make it to the Gulf countries," the IOM statement said.
FIGHTING IN ETHIOPIA Fighting has also broken out in Ethiopia since last month in the [USN:L6N45W02E TEXT:"biggest escalation of violence"] since the 2020-2022 Tigray war.
An IOM official told Reuters that the UN agency had documented heavy migrant traffic along the so-called Eastern Route through Djibouti for several years.
"People continue to use the route amid changing conditions in Ethiopia and Yemen, although the volume and direction of movement can shift over time," the official said.
Ethiopian migrants interviewed as part of the agency's most recent situation report on Djibouti from September 20 to September 30 said they had left their country due to difficult living conditions, including the impact of drought.
"Some migrants also reported that they were fleeing conflict and forced recruitment by armed forces," the report said.
Multiple residents of Tigray, where fighting erupted on September 23, have told Reuters that they had seen Tigrayan rebels forcibly recruit young men into the defence forces. The rebels have denied conducting forced recruitment.
The conflict has sparked fears of a return to all-out war with Ethiopia and Eritrea severing relations over alleged Eritrean support for the rebel alliance seeking to overthrow Ethiopia's government. Eritrea has denied backing the alliance.
SEVERE RISKS The so-called Eastern Route presents many dangers, including accidents at sea, trafficking and arbitrary arrests once on land. In 2025, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along the route, according to IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, as the number of people undertaking the journey increased by 18%.
IOM has described the crisis sparked by the fighting in Yemen as alarming, with displacement figures surging to 200,000 from 76,000 in mid-September, according to data released by the agency last week.
More than 3,700 people have fled Yemen by sea to Djibouti as of last week, it said.

items.title: Saudi Arabia reports injuries in new attack at Riyadh airport, day after strike kills 13
items.author: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari, Yasmine Ghania
items.creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari, Yasmine Ghania
items.summary: The attack comes a day after the deadliest strike on the kingdom in more than a decade killed 13 people and wounded more than 300 at the airport.
items.body:
Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis claimed responsibility for Saturday's strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, as Saudi authorities reported people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.
The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said an "unidentified projectile" had targeted Riyadh's international airport Terminal 4 on Sunday, causing a fire. An unspecified number of people were injured, the Saudi civil aviation authority said, adding it was still assessing the damage.
The coalition also said Saudi air defences had intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of King Khalid International Airport.
The strikes have exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war in Yemen by the Yemeni government against the Iran-aligned group.
The airport has been closed since Saturday's attack. However, a long-planned international energy conference went ahead in Riyadh on Sunday as planned.
HOUTHIS CLAIM RESPONSIBILITY FOR OTHER ATTACKS In a televised speech on Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack and also said the group had attacked the airport in Dammam in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province and two facilities of Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) .
There was no immediate Saudi confirmation. Reuters has reached out to the Saudi media office and to Aramco for comment.
The Houthis earlier on Sunday had renewed their warning to airlines, airport workers, and travellers against using Saudi airports.
"We urge everyone to take our warnings seriously, and Saudi Arabia bears responsibility for any failed interceptions," the group said.
'WORSE IS YET TO COME,' HOUTHIS WARN Saudi Arabia has stepped up its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, launching strikes against the Houthis and backing a Yemeni government counteroffensive after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.
The Houthis said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia carried out 124 air strikes in Yemen in the past 24 hours, including the capital Sanaa and the group's stronghold Saada.
Yemen's Houthi-run foreign ministry said that further Saudi military action in Yemen would trigger a stronger response, adding that its actions would be guided by the principle of reciprocity.
"Unless the Saudi enemy stops its aggression and interference in Yemen, worse is yet to come, God willing," the ministry said in statements carried by Houthi-run Al Masirah television.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war on Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
INTERNATIONAL ENERGY CONFERENCE STILL GOING AHEAD The five-day conference of international energy organizations WPC Energy opened as planned on Sunday at a convention centre some 10 km (6 miles) from the airport.
Meanwhile, a ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum also went ahead on Sunday, with its plenary session to be held behind closed doors, according to a media advisory. No further details were immediately available and it was not clear which ministers joined the meeting.
Italy's energy minister, Gilberto Pichetto Fratin, whose country was co-hosting the event, had said on Friday he would participate remotely via video link.
German officials were trying to organise a return flight for Economy Minister Katherina Reiche, who was in Riyadh to attend the WPC conference and ministers' meeting.
She was supposed to return to Berlin on Monday but the ministry said it appeared likely that her flight would not be able to take off due to the closure of the airport and alternatives were being considered.
Separately, Saudi authorities notified parents that in-person classes at all schools in Riyadh would be suspended and shifted to remote learning from Sunday until Thursday for all students, teachers and administrative staff.
In Saturday's attack, the third on Riyadh's airport in a week, the dead included four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and nationals of the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, Saudi authorities said. India's embassy in Riyadh said on Sunday one of its citizens injured in the attack had died, adding to the initial death toll of 12.
Four people were killed in the two previous attacks on the airport earlier in the week. One of the attacks also caused heavy damage to a Saudi commercial plane parked on the tarmac.

items.title: Smith sets catching record as Australia take firm grip on test
items.author: Mark Gleeson
items.creator: Mark Gleeson
items.summary: Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side finished the third day of the first test with a 139-run lead over hosts South Africa before bad light brought an early close to Sunday's play at Kingsmead.
items.body:
Australia's Steve Smith set a record for most test catches as his side finished the third day of the first test with a 139-run lead over hosts South Africa before bad light brought an early close to Sunday's play at Kingsmead.
Smith took four superb catches to take his test tally to 223, going past the record of 220 held by England's Joe Root.
Two of the catches showed outstanding anticipation as Smith shuffled across a few steps to snag South Africa captain Temba Bavuma and Kyle Verreynne as they both tried reverse sweeps off the spin bowling of Nathan Lyon.
He also produced a flying dive across first slip to break the record and see off the threat of David Bedingham.
His last catch, off Beau Webster, brought South Africa’s innings to a close as they scored 284 in reply to Australia’s first innings of 390.
At stumps, Australia were 33 without loss in their second innings with Nic Maddinson 17 not out and Travis Head scoring 10.
Smith’s heroics were in contrast to his last test appearance in South Africa eight years ago when he was captain of the team embroiled in a ball-tampering scandal and handed a one-year ban.
But the sparse home crowd on Sunday were reminded of the 37-year-old’s skills as he contributed to his side’s handy lead with some extraordinary athleticism.
South Africa face an uphill battle if they are to salvage something from the test with two days’ play remaining.
Their batsmen were guilty of playing loose shots at crucial junctures after resuming the day 27-1 with three wickets falling before lunch, four more in the second session but the last two adding 87 runs before the innings came to a close.
"Every time we looked like getting something going, we lost a wicket and that set us back a bit," said South Africa batting coach Ashwell Prince.
Bedingham top scored with 49 but, like most of his teammates, got out to a rash shot. His was a thick edge off a back-foot drive to a Pat Cummins delivery that saw Smith dive across first slip like a top goalkeeper to snag the ball.
Other batting contributions came from Aiden Markram, who made 37, and tail-enders Simon Harmer (35 not out) and Keshav Maharaj with 34.
Cummins returned figures of 3-54, with two wickets each for Josh Hazlewood, Mitch Starc and Lyon.
"There is still a long way to go but we hope that in the South African second innings, the pitch will deteriorate," said Lyon, whose spin could prove key to the outcome of the game.
All three days of the test have ended early because of bad light stopping play, and extra time will again be added to all three of Monday's sessions.

items.title: Los países de América Latina con las tarifas de electricidad residencial más altas y qué las encarece
items.author: Daniel Salazar Castellanos
items.summary: Dentro de la factura que pagan los hogares en la región también se tienen en cuenta la diferenciación de tarifas por franjas horarias, por estrato socioeconómico y, por su puesto, por niveles de consu ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — Los precios de la electricidad residencial en América Latina y el Caribe siguen presionando la inflación y podrían aumentar aún más por los efectos del fenómeno de El Niño y la guerra en Medio Oriente. La inflación energética anual se ubicó en 7,72% en julio en la región , por debajo del 8,03% registrado un mes antes. Sin embargo, el indicador todavía se mantiene por encima de la inflación total, que fue de 4,17% en julio en la región, según la Organización Latinoamericana y Caribeña de Energía (Olacde). Ver más: La inflación energética cede en América Latina en julio, pero aún supera a la general, según Olacde Según la última edición del Panorama Económico de América Latina y el Caribe del Grupo Banco Mundial , la volatilidad de los precios de la energía podría frenar el proceso desinflacionario y mantener una postura cautelosa de los bancos centrales. Esto prolongaría las elevadas tasas de interés reales, que restringen el crédito y la inversión. Asimismo, el Banco Mundial advirtió que El Niño podría afectar la agricultura y la generación hidroeléctrica, lo que podría provocar aumentos en los precios de los alimentos y la energía. En América Latina y el Caribe, el precio de la electricidad residencial depende principalmente de la matriz eléctrica y de los costos de generación, transmisión, distribución y comercialización. Según Olacde, la generación es el componente más importante, con cerca del 50% del total, seguida de la transmisión y distribución, que representan alrededor del 25%. “Uno de los principales factores que inciden en el precio de la electricidad para el usuario final es el costo de la generación eléctrica, el mismo que a la vez depende de la estructura de la matriz de generación”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea Andrés Rebolledo, secretario ejecutivo de Olacde. Si en dicha matriz tienen mayor participación fuentes primarias de costos nivelados bajos, como las energías renovables, el costo de generación también será bajo. Mientras que en una matriz de generación dependiente de combustibles o de tecnologías de alto costo de inversión y operación, el costo de la energía generada será también alto, anotó. Si la matriz de generación tiene alta dependencia de combustibles importados, el costo de generación será susceptible a la variación de los precios internacionales de dichos combustibles. Se estima que más del 60% de la electricidad generada en América Latina y el Caribe proviene de fuentes renovables. Ver más: Los dos países que impulsarán la producción petrolera de América Latina hasta 2050, según OPEP Los países más destacados son Paraguay (100%), Costa Rica (94%), Brasil (87%), Uruguay (87%), Venezuela (85%), Colombia (80%), Ecuador (78%) y Belice (75%). Según Olacde, los costos de transmisión y distribución también inciden en el costo de la electricidad a consumidor final. Sin embargo, por lo general estos suelen ser más estables que los costos de generación, pues dependen principalmente de la inversión y de los gastos fijos y variables de operación y mantenimiento de las redes de transmisión y distribución. Otros factores de peso son los cargos por pérdidas eléctricas y por potencia disponible. También pesan sobre la tarifa los impuestos, subsidios y aportes a fondos de compensación. Dentro de la factura que pagan los hogares en la región también se tienen en cuenta la diferenciación de tarifas por franjas horarias, por estrato socioeconómico y, por supuesto, por niveles de consumo. Olacde también menciona los cargos por servicios conexos como alumbrado público, cuerpo de bomberos, recolección de basura, entre otros. Según información de GlobalPetrolPrices, el precio promedio de la electricidad en el mundo fue de US$0,179 por kWh para usuarios residenciales y de US$0,172 por kWh para empresas hasta el tercer trimestre de 2026. “Los precios más altos de electricidad residencial se encuentran en Europa, con US$0,260 por kWh, y los más bajos en Asia, con US$0,088″, explica. Por su parte, África (US$0,141), Oceanía (US$0,253), Norteamérica (US$0,158) y Sudamérica (US$0,220) se encuentran en un punto intermedio. Fuente: GlobalPetrolPrices Con relación a sus pares, la gran ventaja comparativa de Paraguay se basa en el hecho de poseer, en condominio con dos países vecinos (Argentina y Brasil), dos grandes centrales hidroeléctricas que tienen un elevado factor de planta, aunque sus embalses sean relativamente pequeños, dijo a Bloomberg Línea el profesor Victorio Enrique Oxilia. “Esto significa que el país posee dos grandes centrales con elevada disponibilidad de energía firme”. El costo de generación depende, en buena medida, de la tarifa que la empresa eléctrica estatal Ande (Administración Nacional de Electricidad) debe pagar a las centrales binacionales Itaipú y Yacyretá. Itaipú, la principal fuente de energía de Paraguay, tiene una tarifa relativamente baja, de US$37 por MWh (megavatio-hora) de energía firme. Ver más: Así logró este país de América Latina generar toda su electricidad con fuentes 100% renovables Asimismo, ofrece condiciones de contratación favorables para la Ande, al menos hasta finales de 2026, explica Oxilia, profesor de la Facultad Politécnica de la Universidad Nacional de Asunción, en Paraguay. “La combinación actual de costos de generación de las tres centrales hidroeléctricas proveedoras del sistema eléctrico paraguayo se encuentra alrededor de 29 USD/MWh, uno de los costos más bajos del hemisferio.”, anotó el académico. “Esto permite que el costo de suministro sea relativamente bajo, aunque las pérdidas eléctricas sean elevadas (principalmente en distribución)”. Por otra parte, en los últimos tiempos, el hecho de vender a mineradoras de activos digitales en condiciones que elevan el factor de carga del sistema y con tarifas razonables también ha colaborado con el equilibrio financiero de la Ande. Sin embargo, “estas condiciones pueden cambiar a futuro: en el sentido positivo (se esperan tarifas más bajas de Itaipú), pero también en el sentido negativo (costos marginales elevados a futuro)”. La incidencia de El Niño en los costos de la electricidad para los consumidores en América Latina va a depender del impacto que el fenómeno tenga sobre todo en los sistemas de generación y transmisión. Este efecto varía según la ubicación de la infraestructura y su capacidad para resistir y adaptarse a las condiciones climáticas adversas. Ver más: El shock energético mundial persiste y obliga a los países a cambiar sus respuestas Por ejemplo, indicó Andrés Rebolledo, si los sistemas de generación se encuentran en zonas de incremento de precipitaciones y tienen un alto componente hidráulico, podrían verse beneficiados hasta cierto punto. Esto ocurriría siempre y cuando no se produzcan eventos extremos como inundaciones, que pongan en riesgo la integridad y operabilidad de las centrales hidráulicas. Un sistema eléctrico que depende principalmente de la generación hidroeléctrica puede verse afectado por las sequías, que reducen la disponibilidad de agua para producir energía. “En todo caso, los mercados más vulnerables ante el fenómeno de El Niño serían aquellos con una matriz de generación eléctrica con alta dependencia del recurso hidráulico”, indicó Rebolledo. En junio de 2026, la generación eléctrica de la región alcanzó los 163 TWh, lo que representó una contracción de 1,8% frente al mes anterior, según Olade. La hidroenergía aportó el 43,2% del total y se reafirmó como “la base estructural del suministro regional”, indicó el organismo. Olacde considera que los países de la región deberían fortalecer sus sistemas eléctricos para reducir la exposición de los consumidores a episodios de precios elevados de la energía. Para reducir la exposición, Olacde propone diversificar la matriz de generación eléctrica, con el fin de incrementar su resiliencia tanto ante eventos climáticos como ante coyunturas internacionales desfavorables. Asimismo, promover programas de uso racional y eficiente de la energía entre los consumidores. De otra parte, realizar una planificación eléctrica optimizada tanto desde el punto de vista energético como económico y ambiental, así como establecer mecanismos de compensación y estabilización de precios de la energía. También ve clave reducir al máximo las pérdidas de energía tanto en los procesos de generación como de transmisión y distribución de la electricidad. Si es necesario, desde Olacde proponen establecer subsidios focalizados para los sectores socioeconómicos más vulnerables. items.title: Indonesia moves 8 endangered orangutans to safety after Borneo fires
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
items.body:
Indonesian authorities and conservation workers successfully moved eight orangutans to a safe location after the endangered primates' homes were destroyed by wildfires in the forests of Borneo, they said on Sunday.
The Southeast Asian nation is battling its most intense wildfires in 11 years, mainly on Sumatra and Borneo islands, and the government has warned the blazes could continue until November, aggravated by the El Niño weather pattern.
Three mother-child pairs and two adolescent male orangutans were among those rescued between August and September from several locations, the Indonesian government and wildlife foundation, Yayasan Inisiasi Alam Rehabilitasi Indonesia (YIARI) said in a statement.
"Their relocation to Batu Nyambu protected forest is expected to give the eight orangutans a chance to return to living naturally," the statement read.
Orangutans are critically endangered great apes found in the wild only on the Southeast Asian islands of Borneo and Sumatra, with Indonesia home to all three recognised species, according to the World Wildlife Fund. Populations have declined due to deforestation, wildfires and poaching.
The relocation operation took six hours by car, one hour on boats, and two more hours on foot, with the orangutans in cages carried on bamboo poles. Before they were moved, YIARI conservationists checked the animals' health.
Since August, the West Kalimantan Natural Resources Conservation Agency and YIARI have rescued 46 orangutans affected by fires, agency head Murlan Dameria Pane said.
From January to July this year, fires burned around 202,000 hectares (500,000 acres) in Indonesia. No official data for subsequent months has been released, but non-governmental organisations estimate fires have burned at least 600,000 hectares more since.
Haze from the fires has caused 175,000 cases of respiratory illness in Indonesia, with the smog affecting neighbouring Singapore and Malaysia where many schools were closed on Friday as air quality deteriorated.

items.title: West Asia war, debt woes top agenda of IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
items.summary: Finance officials gather amid an energy supply shock, rising rates and mounting debt, as World Bank chief Ajay Banga warns of compounding diesel, fertiliser and El Niño risks ...
items.body:
Home / World News / West Asia war, debt woes top agenda of IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok

West Asia war, debt woes top agenda of IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok Finance officials gather amid an energy supply shock, rising rates and mounting debt, as World Bank chief Ajay Banga warns of compounding diesel, fertiliser and El Niño risks

World Bank President Ajay Banga | Photo: Bloomberg

Reuters Bangkok 6 min read Last Updated : Oct 11 2026 | 10:21 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Finance officials from around the world will gather in Thailand this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest energy supply shock ever and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.
  The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, being held outside Washington for the first time in three years.
  Notably absent will be US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handled some "domestic engagements," a US official said.
 

  His decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which the US leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine's battle against Russia's invasion and the US move to impose sanctions on the International Criminal Court.
  World Bank President Ajay Banga told Reuters that while global growth had held up better than feared when Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, shutting off some 20 per cent of the world's oil, pressures were building again. Soaring prices for diesel, rising fertiliser prices and a looming "super" El Niño weather effect that experts say could lead to 450,000 heat-related deaths are all hitting at once.

Also Read

The impact of West Asia's maritime security premium

Markets tumble to 18-month low as US-Iran tensions lift crude oil

Indian airlines cancel Riyadh flights after Houthi missile attack

Domestic refiners shun costly Russian oil as West Asia flows recover

Iran-backed Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi Arabia, Yemen's Aden airport

  Group of Seven countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower petrol prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress.
  Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of US sanctions designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
  More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of the war on February 28, but industry executives say the amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fuelling pressure on prices.

  Banga said the Bank was not revising down its global forecasts at the moment, but was keeping a close eye on developments. "The real thing is not just El Niño by itself; it's the combination ... What's happening to fertilizer prices? What's happening to energy costs? What's happening to debt? It's that put together that creates its own challenges," he said.
  "And I think that will call upon all of us to be far more careful on what we prepare for in the coming months."
  Rising debt
  IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva issued a similar warning in her traditional curtain-raiser speech previewing the meetings, telling the audience, "Winter is coming." The IMF has signalled little change in its forecast for 3 per cent global growth in 2026 and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher. But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia's invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.

  IMF research released on Tuesday showed that sharp spikes in food and energy prices are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability.
  One huge headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War II and will exceed 100 per cent of GDP before 2030.
  Advanced economies, led by the United States, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, El Niño and lack of investment in AI, which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries.

  Emerging market concerns
  Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Interest payments already exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing countries on average.
  Early in the Covid-19 crisis, G20 leaders announced a suspension of debt service payments for the poorest countries, but there is little appetite for such action now, according to diplomats from G20 countries, who said high debt levels and political pressures posed bigger hurdles this time.
  Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programmes that call for fewer but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures.

  "Countries are already cutting their expenditures because their debt payments are going high and because of the IMF conditionality," said Iolanda Fresnillo, who works on debt justice for Eurodad. "We fear that this review of conditionality policy is just going to make things worse." Kenya, she said, had avoided a debt restructuring by cutting public expenditures and trying to raise taxes, but the changes sparked significant protests, especially by young people.
  The IMF risked losing credibility unless it acknowledged the severity of the crisis facing many developing countries.
  "As long as they continue with the governance structure that they have, they are becoming less and less relevant," she said.

  Security and finance
  Flight routes to Bangkok often pass through the Middle East, posing immediate security challenges to the 10,000-plus travellers descending on Thailand's bustling capital city of 9 million residents following recent attacks on Saudi airports.
  The last off-site annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank took place in Morocco just days after militants led by Hamas killed 1,200 people in Israel, followed by Israel's bombardment of Gaza that killed more than 74,000 people and devastated cities throughout the Palestinian area.
  Three years later, the linkage between national security and international finance is clear, although finance officials at the time had dismissed the Hamas attack as not being an economic issue, said Josh Lipsky, vice-president of international economics at the Atlantic Council.

  "Obviously there have been massive global ramifications," he said. "What we're currently experiencing with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has a direct connection with what happened three years ago."
  Policymakers needed to become more agile in responding to geopolitical crises in an increasingly interconnected world, Lipsky said. "They have to be proactive and they have to recognize that they don't live in the world they used to."

items.title: Ukraine-Trump annonce un cessez-le-feu dans l'énergie, Zelensky attend des précisions
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et son entrée en vigueur, avant d'être rapidement contredit par son homologue ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.
items.body:
Le président américain Donald Trump a annoncé dimanche la conclusion d'un accord de cessez-le-feu entre l'Ukraine et la Russie portant sur les infrastructures énergétiques et son entrée en vigueur, avant d'être rapidement contredit par son homologue ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.
"Avec effet immédiat, il y a un CESSEZ-LE-FEU ÉNERGÉTIQUE dans la guerre entre la Russie et l'Ukraine. Les deux parties ont donné leur accord. Ne le violez pas !", a écrit Donald Trump sur son réseau Truth Social.
Quelques minutes plus tard, Volodimir Zelensky a cependant indiqué ne pas avoir été informé d'une telle trêve, déclarant au site d'information Axios que l'annonce du président américain constituait "une surprise" pour lui.
"L'Ukraine soutient le cessez-le-feu, et il est important que la Russie le soutienne également. Nous attendons des précisions de la partie américaine", a-t-il écrit par la suite sur l'application Telegram.
"Pour sa part, l'Ukraine soutient toujours PLEINEMENT les mesures visant à la désescalade, à la protection des vies humaines et aux décisions nécessaires pour mettre fin à la guerre et garantir une paix durable."
Moscou n'a pas commenté les annonces de Donald Trump dans l'immédiat.
Plus tôt, Volodimir Zelensky s'était dit disposé à suspendre les attaques contre les raffineries de pétrole russes si Moscou cessait ses propres frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques ukrainiennes, après que Donald Trump a exigé que Kyiv mette unilatéralement fin à ses assauts.
Il a également déclaré qu'il organiserait des élections en Ukraine si le président russe Vladimir Poutine acceptait un cessez-le-feu global de 60 jours.
Samedi, Donald Trump a imputé la hausse des prix du diesel aux États-Unis aux frappes ukrainiennes contre les raffineries russes et a déclaré que Volodimir Zelensky "ferait mieux d'arrêter immédiatement", ajoutant que l'Ukraine devrait le remplacer à sa tête car il avait laissé passer plusieurs occasions de conclure un accord avec Moscou.
"DITES À POUTINE DE NOUS DONNER DEUX MOIS" La forte hausse des prix mondiaux du diesel, qui a suivi le déclenchement de la guerre avec l'Iran en février, est devenue un handicap politique pour le Parti républicain de Donald Trump à l'approche des élections de mi-mandat du mois prochain, lors desquelles les démocrates pourraient reprendre le contrôle d'une ou des deux chambres du Congrès.
Volodimir Zelensky a réaffirmé dimanche la position de longue date de l'Ukraine, selon laquelle elle est disposée à cesser ses attaques contre les raffineries russes uniquement dans le cadre d'une désescalade réciproque du conflit, qui exigerait que Moscou mette également fin à ses frappes contre les infrastructures électriques ukrainiennes.
Tout accord de ce type devrait s'accompagner de "garanties réelles", a déclaré Volodimir Zelensky.
"La véritable cause de la guerre en Europe, c'est la Russie et la Russie seule", a-t-il dit, sans faire directement référence aux propos de Donald Trump.
"Il est possible de mettre fin aux frappes contre les infrastructures énergétiques dès aujourd'hui, mais Vladimir Poutine ne le veut pas."
"Dites à Poutine de nous donner deux mois, 60 jours de cessez-le-feu total, 60 jours, et nous organiserons des élections", a également déclaré Volodimir Zelensky à la chaîne américaine ABC.
Samedi, il a réagi avec colère à l'annonce par Donald Trump d'un accord d'approvisionnement en diesel avec la Russie, estimant que celui-ci encouragerait les attaques de Moscou contre l'Ukraine.
"UNE TRAHISON" Des analystes ont déclaré que l'accord conclu par Donald Trump avec Moscou avait peu de chances d'entraîner une baisse durable des prix des carburants, les volumes concernés restant bien inférieurs aux exportations habituelles de la Russie lorsque ses raffineries ne sont pas visées par des attaques.
L'accord sur le diesel a également été critiqué par des élus américains, dont le représentant républicain Don Bacon, qui a estimé qu'il était temps de renforcer les sanctions plutôt que de les alléger.
Dans les rues de Kyiv, plusieurs habitants ont fait part de leur colère après la suggestion de Donald Trump selon laquelle l'Ukraine devrait se trouver un nouveau dirigeant prêt à conclure un accord avec le président russe Vladimir Poutine.
"Personne n'a le droit de nous dire ce que nous devons faire, d'autant que des élections ne peuvent pas être organisées en temps de guerre", a déclaré Sabina, une institutrice de 40 ans, en référence à l'interdiction des élections en Ukraine sous le régime de la loi martiale pour des raisons de sécurité.
"À mes yeux, c'est une trahison de la part de nos partenaires", a-t-elle déclaré au sujet des remarques de Donald Trump.
Volodimir Zelensky a déclaré qu'il poursuivrait dimanche ses discussions avec les dirigeants européens et que des échanges avaient lieu quotidiennement sur des dispositifs supplémentaires de défense aérienne, notamment des munitions pour les avions de combat utilisés pour abattre les drones russes à réaction.
Lundi, le ministre ukrainien des Affaires étrangères, Andrii Sybiha, doit participer à une réunion du Conseil des affaires étrangères de l'Union européenne qui devrait examiner un renforcement de la pression des sanctions contre la Russie ainsi que l'avancement des négociations sur l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Union européenne.

items.title: Trump announces Ukraine energy ceasefire with Russia, surprising Zelenskiy
items.author: Daniel Flynn, Steve Holland
items.creator: Daniel Flynn, Steve Holland
items.summary: There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump made a surprise announcement of an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine on Sunday that he said was "effective immediately", but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the deal.
There was no word from Moscow on the announcement, which followed days of intense pressure from Trump for Ukraine to halt its attacks on Russian oil refineries. He blames those strikes for a rise in diesel prices that is hurting his Republican Party ahead of US midterm elections next month.
In a dramatic deterioration in relations, Trump on Saturday warned Zelenskiy that he had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""] attacking Russian refineries, and urged Ukrainians to replace their leader at new elections. Trump said Zelenskiy had missed several opportunities to strike a deal with Moscow.
In a post on his Truth Social platform on Sunday, Trump unexpectedly announced that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, but did not elaborate further.
"Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!" Trump wrote.
Trump, whose war in Iran has been widely blamed for hiking global fuel prices, had previously announced an energy ceasefire in Ukraine in [USN:FWN4560K2 TEXT:"mid-September"], although neither side ever confirmed such an agreement was reached.
Zelenskiy said in a post on the Telegram app that he had discussed Trump's announcement with NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
"Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side," he said.
Hours earlier, Zelenskiy had pushed back against US pressure for a unilateral end to Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, repeating his long-standing position that he was willing to do so only if President Vladimir Putin suspended Russian strikes on Ukrainian power infrastructure.
Any such ceasefire agreement would need to come with "real guarantees", Zelenskiy said.
"The real cause of the war in Europe is Russia and Russia alone," Zelenskiy said. "It's possible to stop strikes on energy infrastructure as early as today, but Putin does not want to do so."
PROMISE OF ELECTIONS Trump also called for elections in Ukraine, suspended since the 2022 Russian invasion, to which Zelenskiy responded that he would call a vote if Putin agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.
Zelenskiy said it was "up to Ukrainians" to choose their leader, but added that there needed to be an end to the fighting first. Ukrainian law [USN:L1N44G089 TEXT:"prohibits elections under martial law"] for security reasons.
"Please tell Putin, give us two months, 60 days of total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organise elections," Zelenskiy said.
The Ukrainian leader rejected that he was to blame for energy price rises, adding that "everybody in the world" knew that the war in the Middle East was a bigger factor.
The steep rise in global diesel prices, which followed the outbreak of the Iran war in February, has become a political liability for Trump's Republican Party ahead of the midterms, when opposition Democrats could gain control of one or both houses of Congress.
On Saturday, Zelenskiy responded angrily to Trump's announcement of a diesel supply deal with Russia, saying it would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine and lead to a greater loss of civilian lives.
Analysts said Trump's diesel supply agreement with Moscow was unlikely to lead to sustained lower fuel prices as the volumes involved were too small.
Under terms of the deal as described by Trump on Friday, Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to US and global markets, equal to about 2.25 million barrels of fuel. The US exports about 1.5 million barrels of diesel per day.
The diesel deal was also criticized by US lawmakers, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions, not lift them.
KYIV RESIDENTS ANGRY On the streets of Kyiv, several residents expressed anger at Trump's suggestion that Ukraine should find a new leader willing to make a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"No one has the right to tell us what to do, especially since elections cannot be held during wartime," said Sabina, a 40-year-old primary school teacher. "In my view, it is a betrayal by our partners," she said, describing Trump's remarks.
Zelenskiy said he would continue discussions with European leaders on Sunday, and there were daily conversations around additional air defence packages, including ammunition for combat aircraft that are used to down Russia's jet-powered drones.
On Monday, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha is due to participate in a European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting that is expected to discuss increasing sanctions pressure on Russia and advancing negotiations on Ukraine's EU accession.

items.title: Gea sends Shelton crashing out of Shanghai
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday.
items.body:
US Open finalist Ben Shelton conceded he had been "outplayed" after suffering a shock 7-6(5) 7-6(3) defeat by France's Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters on Sunday.
World number four Shelton, who has barely played since losing to Alexander Zverev in September's US Open final and withdrew from the Japan Open due to fitness concerns, lost both sets against the world number 56 in tight tiebreakers.
Asked if his recent lack of action had had an effect on him, Shelton told reporters: "I mean, I got outplayed today. The guy played better than me.
"A hundred percent, I would have liked to have come over here earlier and be prepared and have already dealt with the jet lag by the time I was playing here in the Shanghai Masters.
"My body wasn't ready. I wasn't physically ready to play in Tokyo. That's just the way this tour is sometimes."
The 24-year-old American said he was focused on finishing his 2026 campaign on a "high note" at the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin next month.
"Obviously I want to be prepared and playing some of my best tennis when I get there," he added.
"Three tournaments left to finish the year, which has been a very up and down year, but a great year, on a high note."
Gea, who next faces either Jakub Mensik or Francisco Cerundolo, was delighted with his first win over a top-10 player.
"I'm practicing hard every day since the beginning of the year to win against those guys," he said.
"Of course, when you win, it is always special. But, yeah, I was prepared and I was confident before the match. Also playing a really good season right now, so, yeah, that's a really good win, but I was ready for it."

items.title: L'aéroport de Ryad a encore été ciblé, dit la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite
items.author: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.creator: Jana Choukeir, Maha Dahan, Timour Azhari
items.summary: La coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen a annoncé qu'un "projectile non identifié" avait frappé dimanche l'aéroport international de Ryad, provoquant un incendie, au lendemain d'une attaque contre ce même aéroport revendiquée par les Houthis qui a fait 12 morts.
items.body:
La coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen a annoncé qu'un "projectile non identifié" avait frappé dimanche l'aéroport international de Ryad, provoquant un incendie, au lendemain d'une attaque contre ce même aéroport revendiquée par les Houthis qui a fait 12 morts.
Quelques heures auparavant, les Houthis avaient renouvelé leurs mises en garde contre l'utilisation des aéroports saoudiens, appelant les compagnies aériennes, les employés des aéroports et les voyageurs à s'en tenir éloignés.
Le groupe soutenu par l'Iran a déclaré que les aéroports et l'espace aérien saoudiens demeuraient des cibles potentielles d'opérations militaires et a averti que le royaume porterait la responsabilité de toute interception qui échouerait.
La coalition a également indiqué dimanche que les défenses aériennes saoudiennes avaient intercepté un missile de croisière à proximité de l'aéroport international du roi Khaled, sans plus de précisions.
L'aéroport de la capitale saoudienne est resté fermé après l'attaque de samedi, qui a fait 12 morts et plus de 300 blessés, ce qui a constitué la frappe la plus meurtrière de ce type dans le royaume depuis plus d'une décennie, sur fond d'escalade des combats entre les Houthis et les forces gouvernementales yéménites.
La coalition a précisé que l'engin tiré dimanche visait le terminal 4 de l'aéroport, sans fournir davantage d'explications.
L'Arabie saoudite a intensifié ces dernières semaines son implication militaire au Yémen, menant des frappes contre les Houthis et soutenant une contre-offensive des forces gouvernementales après que le groupe s'est emparé le mois dernier de secteurs stratégiques le long de la côte de la mer Rouge.
Le ministère yéménite des Affaires étrangères contrôlé par les Houthis a déclaré dimanche que toute nouvelle action militaire saoudienne au Yémen entraînerait une riposte de plus grande ampleur, ajoutant que ses actions seraient guidées par le principe de réciprocité.
UN IMPORTANT CONGRÈS SUR L'ÉNERGIE MAINTENU À RYAD "Tant que l'ennemi saoudien ne mettra pas fin à son agression et à son ingérence au Yémen, le pire est à venir, si Dieu le veut", a déclaré le ministère dans des communiqués relayés par la chaîne Al Masirah, contrôlée par les Houthis.
Le président Donald Trump a déclaré samedi que les États-Unis envisageaient de participer aux frappes saoudiennes contre les Houthis dans ce conflit, qui constitue une extension de la guerre contre l'Iran déclenchée en février par Washington et Israël.
Ces nouvelles menaces interviennent alors que l'Arabie saoudite a maintenu l'accueil d'un important congrès international de l'énergie à Ryad.
Le ministère saoudien de l'Énergie a annoncé que le 25e Congrès mondial de l'énergie (WPC Energy Congress), d'une durée de cinq jours, avait débuté dimanche avec la participation confirmée de plus de 70 ministres, 300 dirigeants d'entreprises et représentants de plus de 25 organisations internationales du secteur de l'énergie, selon la télévision d'État.
La réunion ministérielle de l'International Energy Forum devait également se tenir dimanche, sa séance plénière étant organisée à huis clos, selon un avis aux médias.
L'attaque de samedi a été la troisième visant l'aéroport de Ryad en une semaine. Parmi les victimes de celle-ci figurent quatre Saoudiens, deux Bangladais ainsi que des ressortissants des États-Unis, de Jordanie, de Palestine, de Syrie, du Soudan et d'Égypte.

items.title: INWIT investors line up financing for possible take-private, sources say
items.author: Elvira Pollina, Amy-Jo Crowley, Valentina Za
items.creator: Elvira Pollina, Amy-Jo Crowley, Valentina Za
items.summary: The leading shareholders in INWIT are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers.
items.body:
The leading shareholders in INWIT (INWT.MI) are arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal of Italy's largest mobile telecom towers company, two people close to the matter said, amid a contractual dispute between the masts firm and its two main customers.
French private equity firm Ardian and investment vehicle Oak Holdings 1, the latter backed by co-investors GIP, Vodafone (VOD.L) and KKR (KKR.N) , are exploring a bid to buy out minority shareholders in INWIT, the people said.
Ardian controls 32% of INWIT, while Oak Holdings controls 39%.
The investors are discussing the financing of the bid with banks, the people said, with one person adding that Abu Dhabi investment firm Mubadala is expected to take a stake in INWIT as part of the plan.
The people cautioned that deliberations are still ongoing.
Ardian, GIP, Vodafone (VOD.L) , KKR (KKR.N) and Mubadala declined to comment. GIP is part of US investment firm Blackrock (BLK.N) .
An INWIT spokesperson said the company did not have any information on the matter.
INWIT, which listed in Milan in 2015, has been the subject of [USN:L6N40C0Y4 TEXT:"takeover speculation"] since a French media report in February that infrastructure fund Ardian and investment group Brookfield were interested in taking the Italian company private.
INWIT has since then become [USN:L8N43G1LQ TEXT:"embroiled in a dispute"] with its two main customers, Telecom Italia (TIM) (TLIT.MI) and Swisscom's Fastweb (SCMN.S) , both of which have initiated procedures to terminate their respective contracts with INWIT as part of efforts to renegotiate them on more favourable terms.
INWIT's market value has fallen about 27% over the past year to $7.1 billion (€6.3 billion) as of Friday's close, according to LSEG data.
(1 euro = $1.1201)
