items.title: Polish police detain man after threat to PM
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Polish police have detained a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk, the Interior Minister said on Sunday, after it warned earlier of a threat to Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.
items.body:
Polish police have detained a man suspected of planning an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk, the Interior Minister said on Sunday, after it warned earlier of a threat to Tusk and Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz.
"The man who threatened and planned an attack on Prime Minister Donald Tusk has been detained by Polish police," Marcin Kierwinski wrote on X, without giving further details.
Tusk thanked the police for "swift and decisive action" in a separate post on X.
While violent crime is relatively rare in Poland, the country is deeply polarised politically and has faced security threats due to its proximity to the war in Ukraine.
In August, police detained a 23-year-old man accused of [USN:L1N44I06W TEXT:"calling for the assassination"] of senior Polish politicians.
In 2024, Tusk said he received threats after an [USN:L1N3W206N TEXT:"assassination attempt"] on Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.
Interior Ministry Spokesperson Karolina Galecka said on Sunday an email with information about the potential attack had been forwarded to police by the State Protection Service, which is responsible for ministers' security.

items.title: From theatre to streets, Gen Z protester Neha Bora a new face of India's youth unrest
items.author: Aftab Ahmed, Saurabh Sharma
items.creator: Aftab Ahmed, Saurabh Sharma
items.summary: The 29-year-old doctoral student said she did not set out to become an activist.
items.body:
A little-known doctoral student has emerged as one of the most visible faces of a protest movement in India that has mounted the most serious challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government in years.
Neha Bora, 29, is one of a number of prominent activists detained this weekend as the authorities cracked down on attempts by protesters led by the "Cockroach" youth movement to demonstrate against what they say is massive vote-rigging to help Modi's party.
But Bora, national president of the left-wing All India Students’ Association, says she did not set out to become an activist. She traces her path into politics to theatre and, later, the student-led protests against a citizenship law in 2019 and 2020.
BORA URGES PROTESTERS ON FROM DETENTION On Saturday, after police blocked demonstrators from reaching New Delhi's designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, Bora urged them to regroup at Dilli Haat, a crafts market 10 km (6 miles) away.
"Dilli Haat becomes Jantar Mantar today," she wrote on X before setting off towards the site, chanting slogans as others followed.
Police detained her with several other activists. But even in detention, she called for the demonstration to continue.
"I am in detention. The movement is not," she said in a video posted online, urging supporters who were stopped by police to protest wherever they were. She was released later on Saturday.
The Cockroach Janta Party-led protests seek the ouster of India's election chief, claiming irregularities in handling voter data have led to the deletion of 130 million names — more than the population of Japan — from electoral rolls.
The Election Commission denies favouring any group, and Modi's Hindu nationalist party has accused opponents of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Other issues Bora has championed include school-examination scandals, unemployment and police actions.
Soft-spoken in conversation but forceful behind a microphone, she has built a following through speeches in Hindi and English, often invoking constitutional rights and linking student grievances to broader questions of inequality and government accountability.
'HOPE IS ALSO INFECTIOUS' Bora grew up in the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand and moved frequently as a child because her father served in the army. She studied at Delhi University before beginning a doctorate at Jawaharlal Nehru University's School of Arts and Aesthetics.
As an undergraduate, she told Reuters in an interview this month, she joined a theatre group, where she learned to inhabit the lives of people much different from herself.
"There might be a character that if you meet in your real life, you will disagree with, you will not like. But to do theatre is to understand where that person comes from."
A turning point was the citizenship law, which critics say discriminates against Muslims.
Bora said she watched students of her own generation lead classmates out of lecture halls and onto the streets, turning ideas she had encountered in books, films and documentaries into political action.
She gained wider attention during protests in July over alleged leaks of exam papers, when she joined other activists in demanding the resignation of the education minister. Her speeches at Jantar Mantar, criticising the government and police response to demonstrators, circulated widely online.
Bora has since become a fixture at demonstrations in the capital. During protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, she was repeatedly detained and returned to the streets after her release.
She said ideology alone does not drive the current mobilisation, describing hope as a more powerful force.
"Fear is infectious, of course. But hope is also infectious," she said. "People have courage now because they think that they can have courage."
Bora said the demonstrations reflect the accumulation of years of grievances.
"People remember," she said. "People carry that discontent, people carry that betrayal, people carry that disappointment."

items.title: Pakistan imposes emergency rule over Imran Khan's provincial government
items.author: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
items.creator: Asif Shahzad, Ariba Shahid
items.summary: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, following allegations by the federal government that it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.
items.body:
Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, following allegations by the federal government that it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.
The constitution allows the federal government to take over some or all provincial government functions during an emergency.
A provincial governor will take charge with an advisory council, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar told a news conference in Islamabad, adding that the arrangement will initially be in place for six months.
The interior ministry said it would be deploying troops in the northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province bordering Afghanistan, which has suffered an increasing number of [USN:L1N43Z03Y TEXT:"militant attacks"] in recent months.
"The situation is so grave that you wouldn't see any residents coming out of their houses after evening in some of the districts," said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi.
The federal government and the military have accused Khan's party of failing to curb the militants, while Khan's party has rejected the accusation and says the federal government has failed to provide it with the funding and equipment needed.
Islamabad accuses neighbouring Afghanistan of harboring Islamist militants who launch attacks inside Pakistan, and says that Khan's party had been sympathizing with both the Taliban in Kabul and their affiliates at home.
Both the Afghan Taliban and Khan's party have denied the accusation.
President Asif Ali Zardari declared an emergency on the advice of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif following a federal cabinet decision, the president's office said.
The security forces and citizens had been under attack for the last two years, Sharif told the Cabinet. "We can't just act a silent spectator."
`COUP DISGUISED AS EMERGENCY` The move comes after Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party rallied for several days to pressure the government for his release, threatening to [USN:L8N45R072 TEXT:"march on the capital"] Islamabad in coming days amid deepening political instability.
Khan's supporters say the military rigged the 2024 election against the 74-year-old former cricket star, an allegation the military denies.
"This is more of a coup disguised as emergency," said Zulfikar Bukhari, Khan's aide and his party's spokesperson, adding that it risks leading to further bloodshed and instability.
Ahead of the planned march, authorities detained three of Khan's sisters and hundreds of party activists. Restrictions have been placed on the movements of Chief Minister, Sohail Afridi of Khan's party, one of his close aides told Reuters.
The government has cut access to the capital, Islamabad, to bar the protesters from reaching parliament, blocking major highways with shipping containers and deploying tens of thousands of security forces, interior ministry officials said.
The party's last large-scale protest two years ago ended in deadly clashes with security forces.
Khan's 2023 arrest sparked nationwide riots that threatened the standing of the Pakistani military. Cases against Khan have ranged from concerns over state gifts to instigating violence and an accusation of an unlawful marriage.
All convictions but one have since been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing.
The latest protest coincides with public discontent over inflation and rising fuel prices that has spread beyond Khan's core supporters.
items.raw_description: Pakistan's president declared a state of emergency and suspended the provincial government of jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan on Sunday, following allegations by the federal government that it has failed to tackle Islamist militancy.

items.title: Bezzecchi pips Fernandez to win Indonesian GP, Martin retakes championship lead
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez.
items.body:
Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi ruthlessly hunted down injured Raul Fernandez to win the Indonesian Grand Prix on Sunday, while Jorge Martin came in third to retake the championship lead from rival Marc Marquez.
[USN:L4N45W00O TEXT:"Polesitter Fernandez"], racing with fractured fingers sustained in a crash on Saturday, looked untroubled in the opening half of the race as he and Bezzecchi surged away from the chasing pack.
But the Trackhouse rider began to fade as the afternoon wore on, and a determined Bezzecchi finally pounced with nine laps remaining to seize the lead and secure victory, with Martin completing a podium lockout for Italian manufacturer Aprilia.
Bezzecchi's win, the 300th victory for an Italian in MotoGP, also kept his faint championship hopes alive.
"I'm very, very happy to be back on the top step of the podium," said the 27-year-old, who led the standings in the early stages of the season but has struggled in recent weeks.
"It was a nice, nice battle with Raul. I think we deserve a result like this, me and all my team, especially them, because they never stop working. They've been through tough times with me."
A dejected Fernandez revealed the full extent of his injury after the race.
"Yesterday, when I crashed and I saw my hand, I knew before going to the clinic that I had my finger broken, the one that normally I used to brake," the Spaniard said.
"This morning, when I woke up, I realised I don't have one, but two fingers broken. No one knew. I tried to say nothing, just keep the pain for me and keep my focus on the race.
"This morning, I tried find a solution on the brakes, because I was not able to use the finger that I use normally. I started everything from zero. It was a very difficult job for me."
MARTIN BACK AT THE TOP The most exciting duel in the race took place behind the top three, with Marquez engaging in a thrilling back-and-forth with KTM's Pedro Acosta.
Marquez had a strong start and swooped into third place in the opening lap, but his Ducati struggled to keep pace with the Aprilia machines around him, and a hard-charging Martin picked him off with ease in the third lap.
The defending champion was then quickly overtaken by Acosta, but for the second time in as many days, Marquez profited from tyre pressure issues for his opponent and was allowed back into fourth.
When Acosta was sure he would not receive a penalty, he once again locked horns with Marquez, but as they traded blows, Trackhouse's Ai Ogura capitalised and moved past both riders to seal a first-ever 1-2-3-4 finish for Aprilia.
Martin, the 2024 champion, moved up to 355 points at the top of the championship standings, with [USN:L1N45W01V TEXT:"Saturday's sprint-winner Marquez"] on 353 points after finishing in sixth place - the first time he has completed a full race at the Mandalika circuit.
"The last few laps, I was struggling a lot with the tyres, physical condition, but I was able to finish on the podium, so really, really happy," Martin said.
"We are still in the fight. We are still in the lead. It will be a tough championship, but I will give my all."

items.title: Hurricanes aim to extend win streak to 5, add to Flyers' woes
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions.
items.body:
Less than two weeks into the season, the Carolina Hurricanes and Philadelphia Flyers are heading in vastly different directions.
The Hurricanes aim for their fifth straight victory Sunday when they visit the winless Flyers for the second consecutive weekend.
Carolina lost its first two games before posting a 3-2 triumph in Philadelphia on Oct. 3. Former Flyer Shayne Gostisbehere scored the overtime winner for the Hurricanes, who used that victory as a springboard to three more wins.
Most recently, Carolina posted a 5-2 road victory over the Chicago Blackhawks on Saturday. Jackson Blake and Jordan Martinook each registered a goal and an assist for the Hurricanes.
"Every single line is contributing," Martinook said. "The 'D' is playing some of the best hockey I've ever seen the group play together. ... It's been fun to watch."
Sebastian Aho added a shorthanded goal for his team-leading fifth goal, while Mark Jankowski and Taylor Hall also scored for the defending Stanley Cup champions.
"We've definitely, after the first couple games, gotten into our game," Aho said. "Just playing Hurricanes hockey, and that usually gives you a chance to win."
The Hurricanes have scored 21 goals during their four-game winning streak. Jankowski has scored in each of the last three games, while Brandon Bussi has earned the victory in each of his last two starts.
"It was a good effort from pretty much everyone," Carolina coach Rod Brind'Amour said. "I liked it. ... When we're going, you can tell we're in sync."
Philadelphia, meanwhile, has lost 10 straight games dating back to its second-round playoff series against Carolina. The Hurricanes swept the Flyers last spring en route to winning the Stanley Cup, and the hangover has continued into the current campaign, as Philadelphia is 0-4-2.
"It's not like we're not trying," said rookie forward Porter Martone, who scored the Flyers' goal in Saturday's 5-1 road loss to the Boston Bruins. "These guys in this group, we care. I think a lot of people from the outside think it's lack of effort, but everyone in this room is giving it their all. We don't like this. We're not having fun right now. We want to win."
Philadelphia has been outshot by a wide margin and outscored 24-7 in its first six games. The Flyers scored only three goals while going 0-2-1 on their three-game road trip that ended Saturday.
The last time the Flyers lost their first six games was in 2008-09, when the team began 0-3-3 before rallying to make the postseason.
"You've got to stick together," said Philadelphia coach Rick Tocchet, whose team played Saturday without forward Travis Konecny and defensemen Rasmus Ristolainen and Cam York. "We're at the bottom. We're in the muck right now. Hopefully, we get some healthy bodies back, but you've just got to stick together. There's no other answer. We've all been, in life, in a situation where you're in a foxhole and we need some people to sit in a foxhole and stick together."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Most Gulf stocks in red after attack on Riyadh airport
items.author: Ateeq Shariff
items.creator: Ateeq Shariff
items.summary: Most Gulf stock markets ended lower on Sunday, as geopolitical concerns weighed on sentiment after an attack on Riyadh's international airport left at least 12 dead and more than 300 wounded, marking the kingdom's deadliest attack in over a decade.
items.body:
Most Gulf stock markets ended lower on Sunday, as geopolitical concerns weighed on sentiment after an [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attack on Riyadh's international airport"] left at least 12 dead and more than 300 wounded, marking the kingdom's deadliest attack in over a decade.
Adding to the uncertainty, Yemen's Houthis on Sunday [USN:L1N45X01E TEXT:"warned airlines, travellers and airport workers to stay away from Saudi airports"].
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI) narrowed early losses to finish 0.2% lower with the country's biggest lender by assets Saudi National Bank (1180.SE) losing 1.1%. Oil major Saudi Aramco (2222.SE) was down 0.2%.
President Donald Trump has said Washington was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Iran-backed Houthis, widening a regional conflict that spilled over from the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Riyadh and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government have claimed hundreds of strikes against targets in Houthi-held territory in Yemen. The Houthis have said these killed civilians including women and children. Reuters could not independently verify those claims.
In Qatar, the benchmark index (.QSI) declined 1.5%, falling for a fourth consecutive session and closing at its lowest since May 2020, with Qatar Islamic Bank (QISB.QA) declining 1.7%.
Geopolitical risks continue to weigh on sentiment, with stalled US-Iran talks constraining risk appetite and reports of renewed escalation adding to caution. Concerns are likely to remain elevated as tanker attacks and maritime disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz persist, said Milad Azar, market analyst at XTB MENA.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30) - which traded after a session's break — declined 2%, with all its constituents closing in negative territory including Commercial International Bank (COMI.CA) , which was down 1.6%.

items.title: Rangers begin life without Igor Shesterkin vs. slumping Canucks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night.
items.body:
The New York Rangers were bracing for the worst when Igor Shesterkin's right skate crashed into the goal post Friday night.
On Saturday, the Rangers found out Shesterkin's season was over, and his absence threatens to derail a promising start for a team coming off missing the playoffs for the past two seasons.
Dylan Garand will step in as the 2021-22 Vezina Trophy winner's replacement for the time being, and the Rangers hope his promise in limited action translates to success in regular work starting Sunday night when they host the Vancouver Canucks.
Shesterkin, 30, was injured when his right skate collided with the goal post while sliding into position to make a save with 11:40 remaining in the second period of Friday's 3-1 loss at Washington, which halted a four-game winning streak.
Shesterkin's season is over after he was 3-1-0 with a 1.79 goals-against average. The Rangers are now counting on Garand, who is 3-1-1 with a 1.31 GAA in five career games.
"You never want to see guys get injured, especially your best player in Igor," Garand, 24, told reporters at practice Saturday. "He means a lot to the guys in this room and a lot to me personally. ... I'm excited for the opportunity. Going to put my heart and soul on the line for these guys and this city every night and just try to help the team win."
Garand began this season third on New York's depth chart and was exposed to waivers before getting claimed. He is being elevated because Joonas Korpisalo is out for at least four more weeks due to a lower-body injury. Garand's backup will be journeyman Spencer Martin, who made six appearances last season when Shesterkin was injured in January and went 1-3-0 with a 4.13 GAA.
"A guy (Shesterkin) that means so much to our team," defenseman Adam Fox told reporters at practice Saturday. "Obviously, still processing that and you still feel terrible. Personally having dealt with injuries the past few years and him, too, it (stinks) when you're not able to be out there and help the team. He's such an important piece to this team. It's an opportunity for everyone else to step up."
The Rangers are hoping Garand can help them open a season 4-0 at home for the first time since 2009-10 after outscoring Tampa Bay, Utah and the Islanders 14-5.
Vancouver has allowed a league-leading 29 goals through its first six games, including 14 in a three-game skid against the Vegas Golden Knights, Carolina Hurricanes and New Jersey Devils. The Canucks have permitted 98 shots on goal in their past three games, and have allowed three power-play goals apiece in the past two games.
"From a work ethic standpoint, it just needs to be much more difficult for teams to recover pucks and get to their sets," first-year coach Manny Malhotra said of Vancouver's penalty-killing woes.
Last season, the Canucks had the NHL's worst penalty-kill percentage at 71.5%.
"That's a couple games in a row where our penalty kill has to bear down and get those kills," Vancouver forward Brock Boeser said after taking a pair of penalties against the Devils. "We got to stay out of the box, myself included."
--Field Level Media

items.title: FII selloff intensifies! Foreign investors sell Indian equities worth Rs 45,000 crore in just 6 sessions
items.author: Debaroti Adhikary
items.summary: Foreign investors sold Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in October's first six sessions, nearly matching September's outflows. Elevated US bond yields and crude oil prices continue to pressure markets, while inflation data and geopolitical developments could influence the selling trend.
items.body: FII selloff has intensified in October, with foreign investors net selling Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in just six sessions in October so far, nearly the same as the total Rs 45,536 crore outflows recorded in the entire month of September. Analysts have listed factors that could change the trend and ease pressure on the market.The Indian stock market snapped a record eight-week-long losing streak last week, ending with gains despite strong upswings and downswings. Yet, FIIs remained bearish and continued selling Indian equities in every session so far in October. The foreign investors have remained net sellers of Indian equities for 11 consecutive sessions since mid-September.What's behind the massive FII outflows?The sharp FII selloff came as bond yields soared to multi-year highs, making the risk-free returns from the debt market more lucrative than equities. The 10-year US Treasury yield recorded its biggest quarterly increase of the 21st century in the three months ended September, Reuters reported. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries climbed above 5.3%, surpassing its 2007 peak and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that the rapid acceleration in FII outflows in October so far has taken the total FPI equity selling in 2026 to a whopping Rs 3,60,952 crore. “This massive FPI selling is the primary reason why the Indian market is underperforming this year with negative 13.87% Nifty returns so far in 2026,” he said.Also read | D-St Exit Rush! Sectors that saw sharpest FII selloff in 2nd half of SeptemberWhen can the trend reverse?From the FPI perspective, the rationale behind the massive outflows is the risk-free return from the 10-year US bonds being above 5.2%, according to the analyst. “So long as the US bond yields remain elevated, FPIs will continue to sell. The scenario will change when the valuations become attractive, and the risk-reward ratio turns favourable for investment,” Vijayakumar explained.Over the last two months, the market has been steadily trending down. Elevated crude prices and high US bond yields are the two headwinds for the market now, he added, warning that so long as these headwinds remain strong, the market will remain under pressure.Going ahead, investors will closely track US and Indian inflation data, US bond yields, Brent crude prices and developments in US-Iran geopolitical tensions in the coming week, according to Pabitro Mukherjee, Deputy Vice President of Research at Bajaj Broking.Also read | FIIs dump Indian stocks for eight straight weeks: Is a reversal on the cards or more pain ahead?Technical view on NiftyGoing forward, the 22,350–22,330 zone could act as immediate support for Nifty, according to Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities. He noted that a decisive move below this zone could trigger renewed selling pressure towards 22,200.On the upside, the 22,660–22,680 zone, coinciding with the 10-day EMA, could act as an immediate hurdle, according to the analyst, who feels that a sustained move above this zone could trigger short covering and extend the pullback towards 22,820. Despite the recent recovery, confirmation through sustained buying remains necessary, he warned.Also read | Nifty bulls regain momentum, but can bears strike back? 5 factors to decide D-Street’s fate next weekDisclaimer: This article has been written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. BENGALURU, Oct 11 : Elon Musk said he would price Starlink's satellite internet service affordably in India to take on Mukesh Ambani's low-cost Reliance Jio, escalating his attacks on the rival billionaire days before Jio's parent launches India's largest-ever IPO.
Jio Platforms, which owns the telecom arm, is targeting a valuation of $106 billion in the offering. Much like SpaceX-owned Starlink, Jio's own satellite venture is also awaiting final security clearance to launch.
Cheap data is the playbook that built Jio in India, and the one Musk has used in markets like Kenya to unsettle local telecom players. SpaceX now plans to enter the mobile carrier market itself, starting in the US.
Musk did not specify prices for India, where mobile data costs about 8 cents per gigabyte, among the lowest in the world.

"Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable," he said in a post on his social media platform X on Saturday.
"The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," Musk added.
'PRIME MINISTER AMBANI'
The billionaire's remarks were the latest in a series of X posts where he accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and Ambani of stalling Starlink's entry into one of the world's biggest internet markets to favour market leader Jio.
The posts have marked a sharp turn for Musk, who has long enjoyed a warm public rapport with Modi.
India's government has denied any bias in its approval process, noting that the three satellite ventures seeking to launch, including Starlink's and Jio's, are all awaiting final security clearance.
Late on Friday, Musk taunted Ambani directly, addressing him as "Prime Minister Ambani" and asking whether he would "consider allowing Starlink to compete".
Reliance has not responded to requests for comment on Musk's remarks.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ニューデリー １１日 ロイター] - インドの首都ニューデリーは１１日、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める若者らの抗議活動が２日目を迎えるのを前に警戒が続いている。裁判所は、警察が前日拘束した若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」創設者アビジート・ディプケ氏ら幹部３人の釈放を命じた。

ニューデリーでは１０日、有権者名簿の見直しを巡り、選挙管理委員長の辞任を求める数千人規模の抗議集会が予定されていた。当局は集会を阻止するため市中心部を封鎖。ディプケ氏らはデリーに到着した航空機から降りる際に拘束された。

ＣＪＰの法務責任者ラトナ・シン氏は、ディプケ氏らが今後１年間、治安を乱さないことを条件に釈放されたとＸに投稿した。ソーシャルメディアで著名な活動家ドルーブ・ラティ氏も拘束されていたが、内務省当局者によると、今後の抗議活動に参加しないことを条件に１１日未明に釈放された。

警察は１０日、２０００人以上を拘束。１１日も数千人の警察官や準軍事組織要員を市内各地に配置した。１０日に拘束された人の大半は同日夜までに釈放された。

野党やモディ政権の批判勢力は、抗議参加者に対する当局の対応は強権的だと批判。国連機関も平和的な集会の権利を保障するようインド当局に求めた。

インド外務省は１１日、国連の対応を批判し、声明は「インドの内政への不当な干渉だ」と反発した。

抗議活動では、有権者名簿の見直しがモディ首相の与党インド人民党（ＢＪＰ）に不当に有利に働いているとして、ギャネシュ・クマール選挙管理委員長の辞任を求めている。選管とＢＪＰはこうした指摘を否定している。

items.title: Starlink pricing must be affordable in India, says Musk amid Jio row
items.summary: Musk's comments on X, part of a larger post, come as Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Reliance Industries, counts down to what is expected to be India's biggest public offering ...
items.body:
Home / Technology / Tech News / Starlink pricing must be affordable in India, says Musk amid Jio row

Starlink pricing must be affordable in India, says Musk amid Jio row Musk's comments on X, part of a larger post, come as Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Reliance Industries, counts down to what is expected to be India's biggest public offering

Tech trillionaire Elon Musk (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 11 2026 | 7:22 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Tech trillionaire Elon Musk has said Starlink's pricing in India would have to be made affordable, since no one would buy it if it were too expensive, and argued that competition would give consumers more choice.
Musk's comments on X, part of a larger post, come as Jio Platforms, the digital arm of Reliance Industries, counts down to what is expected to be India's biggest public offering.
"The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business," Musk said.
 

Musk added: "And, obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable."   In the same post, Musk renewed his attack on Mukesh Ambani over Starlink's entry into India, accusing the billionaire's supporters of indulging in "absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole" in arguing simultaneously that his satellite internet service cannot compete with "amazing low prices offered by Ambani's de facto monopoly in India", and claiming - in the same breath - that it poses a strong competitive threat.
"On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn't possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani's de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor! This is absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole," Musk wrote, claiming that the "ridiculous arguments" by Ambani's online supporters made no sense to him.

Also Read

Elon Musk vows affordable Starlink in India ahead of record Jio IPO

Terrafab plant will 'make chips better than anyone', says Elon Musk

Musk slams Ambani supporters for 'hypocrisy' over Starlink's entry in India

Elon Musk shares reports of Reliance-backed firms' donations to BJP

Best of Opinion: Elon Musk should never get a satellite licence in India

The latest post comes amid Musk's scathing criticism of Ambani, over what he saw as a persistent delay in the launch of Starlink satellite broadband services in India.
Reliance has not publicly responded to Musk's allegations, while the government has maintained that the country's authorisation framework for telecom and satellite services is "fair and non-discriminatory" and that any suggestion that it was being applied selectively is "baseless and misconceived".
At the India Mobile Congress this week, as Musk's dramatic confrontation and swipes played out on X in the backdrop of India's swanky annual showcase of its telecom prowess, Reliance Jio Infocomm Chairman Akash Ambani declined to comment on the ongoing debate over satellite communication services, saying the company was focused on delivering value to Indian consumers.

On Friday, Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia asserted that India does not permit monopolies in any sector, and that despite the buzz around one particular company, three players - in fact - have received satcom licences and can start operations after meeting the security requirements and milestones.
Three entities - Musk's Starlink, Reliance Jio's satellite venture Jio Satcom, Bharti-backed Eutelsat OneWeb - have already secured licences, while Amazon's Project Kuiper has expressed interest and will need to follow the established procedure.
Jio is building a satellite constellation of more than 1,600 low-Earth orbit satellites, supported by 23 ground stations. Starlink, operated by Musk's SpaceX, has more than 11,000 satellites in its constellation.

Musk's relentless attacks on Ambani come at a crucial time.
The initial public offering of Jio Platforms, which is expected to be the country's biggest issue, is likely to open for subscription on October 21.
The market expects shares of the digital services major to be listed on the stock exchanges on October 28.
While the company has not formally announced the key dates yet, the mega issue - it is learnt - will open for subscription from October 21 to October 23 after completion of the anchor round on October 19.
At an estimated issue size of USD 3.8 billion, the Jio Platforms' IPO is touted as India's largest public offer.

The company has concluded overseas roadshows and is expected to file final papers with market regulator Sebi for the IPO in the week starting October 12.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) issued its final observations on August 28. Jio Platforms had filed its draft IPO papers in June.
According to its draft prospectus, the company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, equivalent to about 2.9 per cent of its post-issue equity base.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief
items.author: CNA
items.summary: Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
items.body:

Indian capital braces for second day of protests against poll chief

Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across New Delhi on Sunday (Oct 11) although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.

Security personnel are seen at a blocked road amid ongoing protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter roll irregularities, near Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Sajjad Hussain)

FAST

NEW DELHI: New Delhi braced for a second day of youth protests demanding the resignation of India's election chief on Sunday (Oct 11), as a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other senior leaders.
Dipke, the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) , and the other leaders were detained when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
They were produced in front of a magistrate early on Sunday.
"Condition - no breach of peace for one year," the CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said in a post on X announcing their release.

Activist and social media influencer Dhruv Rathee, who was also among those detained, was released past midnight on condition he did not participate in any further protests, said an interior ministry official who declined to be named.

Related:

Indian police detain Cockroach Janta Party founder ahead of youth protest

India detains thousands, locks down Delhi to foil election chief protest

Police detained more than 2,000 people and locked down Delhi's city centre to thwart Saturday's protest, and thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across the city on Sunday although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were back up.
Most of those detained on the first day of protests were released late on Saturday night, police said.
Opposition parties and critics of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.
India's foreign ministry said on Sunday the UN's approach was "selective" and its statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India."

A man rides a scooter past shuttered shops in a deserted market, on the second day of a protest by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Bhawika Chhabra)

MILLIONS OF NAMES REMOVED FROM ELECTORAL ROLL The protests are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a revision of voter lists that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has been in power for more than 12 years.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

Commuters cross a checkpoint as police officers stand guard on the second day of a protest planned by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) seeking the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, in New Delhi, India on Oct 11, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Priyanshu Singh)

Election Commission data cited by the party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
The cockroach party, which began as an online satire, rapidly evolved into a pressure group, with street protests against exam paper leaks culminating in the resignation of Modi's education minister.
The CJP has called its protests against Kumar "Season 2" on its social media handles, and said it would not stop until India's election system was reformed.

items.title: 債務増大や金利上昇が焦点、世銀・ＩＭＦ総会12日から　エネルギー供給に懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。

年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。
items.body:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １１日 ロイター] - 各国の財務・金融当局者が今週、タイのバンコクに集まり、世界銀行と国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）の年次総会に臨む。中東やウクライナの戦争が収束せず、エネルギー供給の混乱や金利上昇が世界経済の重荷となる中、その影響と対応が焦点となる。

年次総会は１２─１８日に開催される。 期間中には２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）や主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の財務相・中央銀行総裁会議も開かれる。イランとの戦争が８カ月目に入り、エネルギー高によるインフレや公的債務の増大が議論の中心になる見通し。 

今年のＧ２０議長国を務める米国のベッセント財務長官は欠席し、財務省高官２人を派遣する。米政府当局者によると、国内で予定があるという。ウクライナ戦争や米国による国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）への制裁を巡って各国間の緊張が高まる中、ベッセント氏がＩＭＦ・世銀総会に加えてＧ２０会合も欠席することに、各国から不満が出る可能性がある。

世界銀行のアジェイ・バンガ総裁はロイターに、イランによるホルムズ海峡封鎖後も世界経済は懸念されたほど悪化していないものの、再び下押し圧力が強まっていると指摘した。

世界の石油供給の約２割が途絶し、軽油や肥料の価格が上昇。Ｇ７は軽油と原油計１億バレルを緊急備蓄から放出することで合意した。トランプ米大統領は１０日、ロシアから軽油の供給を受けることで合意したと発表し、対ロ制裁も一時的に免除する。この決定にはウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領が強く反発した。

２月２８日の戦争開始以降、１０億バレルを超える石油が主に民間在庫から市場に放出されたが、業界幹部によると、世界市場に供給可能な在庫は減少しており、価格上昇への市場の脆弱性が増している。

バンガ氏は、エルニーニョ現象に加え、肥料価格やエネルギーコスト、債務問題が重なることが世界経済のリスクになるとして、今後数カ月に備え「一段と慎重になる必要がある」と述べた。ＩＭＦのゲオルギエワ専務理事も年次総会を前にした講演で「冬が来る」と警告した。

ＩＭＦは２０２６年の世界経済成長率を３％程度とする見通しを大きく変更しないもようだが、ウクライナや、イランの攻撃を受けエネルギー輸出が大幅に減少した湾岸諸国などは下方修正が予想される。

もう一つの大きな懸念は公的債務の増大だ。世界の公的債務は第２次世界大戦後で最高水準にあり、２０３０年までに世界の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）の１００％を超える見通し。新興国や低所得国では米金利上昇に伴う資本流出も重荷となっている。

途上国では利払い費が政府歳入の平均１０％をすでに超え、より高い金利での債務借り換えを迫られている。新型コロナ禍ではＧ２０が最貧国の債務返済猶予に動いたが、今回は同様の措置への機運は乏しい。

米シンクタンクのアトランティック・カウンシルで国際経済部門を統括するジョシュ・リプスキー氏は 、安全保障と国際金融の結び付きが一段と強まっていると指摘。地政学的危機が世界経済に急速に波及する中、政策当局は「もはや以前と同じ世界ではないことを認識しなければならない」と話す。

items.title: Trump promociona megaproyectos ante votantes que se quejan del precio de la gasolina y los alimentos
items.author: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Josh Wingrove
items.summary: Las promesas de proyectos como una planta siderúrgica en Iowa, una fundición de aluminio en Oklahoma y un gasoducto en Alaska se enfrentan a importantes dudas e incertidumbres.
items.body: Bloomberg — Desde hace tiempo, los presidentes han hecho promesas grandilocuentes a los votantes en sus llamamientos electorales de última hora. Ver más: Carney aprovecha la guerra comercial con Trump para acelerar la transformación económica de Canadá Ahora, esa estrategia se está aplicando con toda su fuerza de cara a las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de noviembre, mientras el presidente Donald Trump recorre el país de un extremo a otro promocionando megaproyectos prometidos por valor de miles de millones de dólares en los estados clave y atribuye a su política arancelaria el mérito de haber marcado el inicio de una era dorada para la industria manufacturera nacional. Sin embargo, las promesas de una planta siderúrgica en Iowa, una fundición de aluminio en Oklahoma y un gasoducto en Alaska, tan ansiado desde hace tiempo, se enfrentan a importantes interrogantes, lo que deja sin aclarar si los proyectos se materializarán plenamente o si no serán más que un espejismo de las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Y aunque Trump apuesta fuerte por el largo plazo —aprovechando sus décadas de experiencia como promotor inmobiliario y empleando una táctica utilizada por otros gobernantes en el cargo antes de la jornada electoral—, el riesgo es que esas promesas llamativas resulten vacías para unos votantes más centrados en los gastos cotidianos y en las preocupaciones económicas inmediatas. La fundición prevista para Inola, Oklahoma, pone de relieve ese escepticismo. La empresa Century Aluminum Co., con sede en Chicago, y la empresa estatal de Dubái Emirates Global Aluminium PJSC afirman que sería la primera planta nueva de EE.UU. en casi medio siglo dedicada al procesamiento de aluminio a partir de materia prima. Trump, durante una gira de campaña la semana pasada, afirmó que sería “la mayor fábrica de aluminio, quizás, del mundo”. Pero, incluso en Oklahoma —un estado de mayoría republicana—, el proyecto se enfrenta a la oposición de los residentes, y el Consejo de Administración de Inola impuso una moratoria para bloquear la iniciativa. Century y EGA aún no han tomado una decisión definitiva sobre la inversión, ya que están solicitando propuestas para servicios de diseño de ingeniería y tratando de superar los obstáculos relacionados con la obtención de permisos. La empresa conjunta declaró en un comunicado que se sentía decepcionada por la prórroga de la moratoria impuesta por el municipio y calificó de prematura la propuesta de prohibición de la producción de aluminio. No obstante, Century también ha documentado numerosos riesgos que podrían paralizar el proyecto, reconociendo en su informe anual de 2025 que, incluso con el apoyo del Departamento de Energía, los promotores necesitan “una financiación adicional sustancial” para hacer realidad el proyecto. Algunos de los proyectos previstos ya cuentan con ayudas procedentes de los contribuyentes estatales y federales. Tómese como ejemplo la planta siderúrgica de US$15.000 millones en Iowa, un estado en el que la carrera por el Senado está muy reñida y en el que tres distritos republicanos de la Cámara de Representantes podrían cambiar de color. La planta se beneficiará del apoyo del Banco de Exportación e Importación de EE.UU., que ayudó a financiar una nueva mina en Minnesota para abastecer a la instalación —la primera de este tipo que se inaugura en más de cinco décadas—. Y la semana pasada, la gobernadora republicana de Iowa, Kim Reynolds, firmó una ley que destina hasta US$1.400 millones en incentivos fiscales para la acería. Flanqueado por republicanos de Iowa, Trump describió la planta como una consecuencia de sus políticas comerciales, insistiendo en que “todo el mundo está construyendo sus plantas aquí porque no quieren pagar aranceles”. Aunque Trump afirma que sus políticas están devolviendo la producción a EE.UU., cada uno de los proyectos requiere “alguna ayuda especial del Gobierno para poder llevarse a cabo”, señaló Douglas Holtz-Eakin, presidente del American Action Forum. “No es que la situación económica sea tan buena en todas partes como para que la gente esté construyendo cosas”. También se han planteado dudas sobre el historial de quiebras y reestructuraciones en las que se han visto implicadas unidades del Grupo Essar, el conglomerado indio que está desarrollando el complejo siderúrgico. Una filial de Essar que pretendía desarrollar una mina de taconita en Minnesota se acogió al Capítulo 11 en 2016, y una empresa siderúrgica en Canadá obtuvo protección frente a los acreedores un año antes. Minnesota también rescindió los contratos de arrendamiento de Mesabi Metallics, respaldada por Essar, tras afirmar que la empresa no había cumplido sus compromisos financieros. Por otra parte, Mesabi ha demandado a un competidor por lo que alega que es una conducta anticompetitiva, y el juicio está previsto para el próximo año. Essar ha hecho hincapié en su firme compromiso de invertir en EE.UU., asegurando en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico que su proyecto de acería “se completará con éxito” y beneficiará tanto a Iowa como a Minnesota. “A día de hoy, todo va según lo previsto para que el proyecto se lleve a cabo, lo que lo convertirá en la mayor inversión en una planta siderúrgica de nueva construcción en Estados Unidos, gracias a esta inversión de US$18.000 millones”, afirmó la empresa. Un funcionario de la Casa Blanca señaló que el proyecto de Iowa cuenta con una sólida financiación y destacó los éxitos anteriores de Essar, entre los que se incluyen la puesta en marcha de puertos, la gestión de centrales eléctricas y la explotación de una planta de pellets de hierro en la India. Alaska también ha acaparado una mayor atención por sus ambiciosos planes de construcción. La semana pasada, Trump anunció una inversión surcoreana de US$54.000 millones destinada a un proyecto, estancado desde hace tiempo, para exportar gas natural licuado desde dicho estado. “Cerramos grandes acuerdos”, afirmó. La iniciativa para transportar gas natural desde la vertiente norte de Alaska y licuarlo para su exportación lleva décadas gestándose, frenada por su elevado coste y los retos técnicos que plantea la construcción de un gasoducto que atraviese el estado. Trump calificó el compromiso surcoreano de “irrefutable” y elogió la ayuda del senador Dan Sullivan, un republicano de Alaska que se encuentra inmerso en una reñida campaña de reelección. Horas más tarde, Corea del Sur protestó enérgicamente. El ministro de Industria, Kim Jung-kwan, afirmó que la inversión del país en el proyecto de GNL dependería de su viabilidad comercial. Se trató de una reprimenda sorprendente por parte de un aliado de EE.UU. —uno que se ha comprometido a invertir US$350.000 millones a cambio de una reducción de los aranceles sobre las exportaciones—. Y provocó la reacción de Trump, quien amenazó con imponer aranceles más elevados a los productos surcoreanos si estos se retiraban del proyecto. “El presidente Trump comenzó a aplicar una agenda económica agresiva y favorable al crecimiento desde el primer día, lo que ha supuesto y sigue suponiendo logros tangibles para el pueblo estadounidense”», afirmó el portavoz de la Casa Blanca, Taylor Rogers. “Cuenta con un historial demostrado a la hora de conseguir inversiones históricas, crear puestos de trabajo bien remunerados y recuperar la industria manufacturera para Estados Unidos”. Los estadounidenses, por su parte, están expresando una profunda preocupación por el elevado coste de la vida, lo que convierte la asequibilidad en el tema dominante de las elecciones. Aunque Trump suele hacer alarde de las ganancias en el mercado de valores, el auge de las cuentas 401(k), el aumento del empleo en general y las nuevas promesas de inversión, otros indicadores muestran una economía menos optimista. La elevada inflación llevó a la Reserva Federal a subir los tipos de interés el mes pasado y los costes del combustible se han disparado en medio de las guerras en Ucrania y Oriente Medio. Los tipos hipotecarios se encuentran en el nivel más alto del segundo mandato de Trump. El desempleo sigue siendo históricamente bajo, pero repuntó el mes pasado, y el crecimiento salarial ha sido más débil de lo que esperaban los economistas. “Están buscando a toda prisa formas de demostrar que cuentan con un programa económico sólido, por lo que van por ahí repitiendo: ‘Vienen puestos de trabajo, vienen puestos de trabajo’”, afirmó Sameera Fazili, subdirectora del Consejo Económico Nacional bajo el mandato del expresidente Joe Biden. “Por desgracia para ellos, eso no es lo que más preocupa a los votantes en esta campaña electoral”. Trump no es el único que busca impulsar su campaña electoral presentando proyectos emblemáticos. Antes de las elecciones intermedias de 2022, Biden celebró la puesta en marcha de las obras de una planta de Intel Corp ( INTC ) en Ohio. La construcción sigue en marcha, pero Intel ha retrasado su calendario. Trump también lo ha hecho antes. Antes de las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de 2018, celebró los planes de Foxconn Technology Group de construir una planta de US$10.000 millones en Wisconsin, alardeando de que sería “la octava maravilla del mundo” y crearía 15.000 puestos de trabajo. Foxconn acabó recortando su compromiso de inversión en aproximadamente un 90% y, en última instancia, solo contrató a una fracción de la plantilla prevista. Un funcionario de la Casa Blanca señaló varios anuncios de proyectos de la primera legislatura de Trump que se han llevado a cabo, entre ellos una fábrica de LG Electronics Inc en Tennessee y unas instalaciones de Samsung Electronics Co en Carolina del Sur. Trump ha reconocido los largos plazos a los que se enfrentan este tipo de proyectos. No está claro si el electorado se mostrará paciente. “Quiero que se acuerden de mí dentro de cuatro o cinco años, cuando este país esté en pleno auge”, afirmó Trump en su convención de mitad de mandato celebrada en septiembre. “Recuerden: yo soy quien lo puso en marcha”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Protesters seeking India election chief's ouster detained, as 'cockroach' leaders released
items.author: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Arpan Chaturvedi, Shilpa Jamkhandikar
items.creator: Saurabh Sharma, Sarita Singh, Arpan Chaturvedi, Shilpa Jamkhandikar
items.summary: Youth protesters, many of them from student organizations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests around the city on Sunday afternoon before police hauled them away in vehicles.
items.body:
Police detained hundreds of protesters in Delhi for a second day on Sunday as sporadic protests broke out demanding India's election chief quit, while a court ordered the release of "cockroach" movement founder [USN:L1N45W01X TEXT:"Abhijeet Dipke"] and two other senior leaders.
Dipke and the other leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a nationwide youth protest movement, were [USN:L1N45W00K TEXT:"detained"] when their plane landed in Delhi on Saturday as the movement planned to gather thousands of people at Jantar Mantar in Central Delhi.
The court ordered their release with an undertaking to "maintain public peace", the CJP said in a statement.
The youth movement, which has mobilised protests in recent months against a range of issues from government school infrastructure to jobs for young people, is one of the biggest political challenges to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in his 12 years in power.
The protesters are calling for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar"] over a [USN:L1N45V037 TEXT:"revision of voter lists"] that critics say disproportionately benefits Modi.
NEW PROTESTS IN DELHI, OTHER CITIES Youth protesters, many of them from students organisations affiliated with India's communist parties, launched sporadic protests on Sunday afternoon in Delhi before police detained them and hauled them away in vehicles.
Small protests by dozens of people were also held in the cities of Mumbai, Kolkata, Panaji and Pune, local media reported.
Abhita Ruheja, a protester who was detained on Sunday, said the authorities had turned Delhi into a fortress.
"Is this how a democracy works? They have been scrapping rights after rights and this is turning into a dictatorship," she said.
The All India Students' Association alleged in a post on X that those detained in Delhi were assaulted by police inside the vehicles.
A video posted on X by the Communist Party of India (Marxist) showed one of its lawmakers, John Brittas, who was briefly detained, being helped from a bus to an autorickshaw as he appeared to be in distress.
Reuters could not verify claims about detainees being assaulted by police.
WE WILL HIT THE STREETS AGAIN, DIPKE SAYS Police also detained several journalists covering the protests, many of whom were carrying microphones and had their press cards prominently displayed, according to a Reuters witness.
A Delhi Police spokesperson did not respond at a media briefing to questions about the alleged assaults and detentions.
CJP's Dipke said he was going back to his home in India's western state of Maharashtra as his grandmother had died but added that the protests would continue.
"Haven’t signed any bond that says we won’t protest. We will hit the streets again," he said in a post on X.
Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel continued to be deployed across Delhi, although metro stations reopened and mobile internet services were restored after authorities locked down the city in an attempt to thwart Saturday's protests.
The police spokesperson said 2,400 people were detained on Saturday and most were released the same night.
Opposition parties and critics of Modi's government criticised what they said was the high-handed use of force against the protesters, while a UN body called on authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly was respected and fulfilled.
India's foreign ministry said the UN's statement constituted "an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India".
POLL PANEL, BJP DENY MANIPULATION ALLEGATIONS At an unusually packed hearing on a Sunday, the Supreme Court recorded the government's assurance that lawyers and journalists would not be impeded while performing their duties.
Lawyers protesting outside the Supreme Court were detained briefly on Saturday, as were several reporters including a Reuters journalist.
Sporadic protests have been going on across India since the Indian Express newspaper in late September reported that Kumar's two deputies had raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
The Election Commission says differing views are normal in internal deliberations, and has denied favouring any party.
Election Commission data shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 28 million people who had died, 63 million who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.
Modi's BJP has accused groups opposed to it of trying to undermine the country's democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes. The Election Commission has said that voters wrongly deleted can re-enrol.
The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties allege Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.

South Korea completes Arctic-Europe commercial voyage, eyes regular service despite risks

South Korean President President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030.

The PanStar Acro, South Korea's first such commercial voyage to Europe via the Arctic, make its way to the port of Felixstowe, in Felixstowe, Britain on Sep 11, 2026. (File photo: Reuters/Chris Radburn)

FAST

SEOUL: A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday (Oct 11), as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub.
The PanStar Acro docked in the southeastern port 50 days after setting sail on Aug 22. Authorities say the Arctic route could cut typical voyage times by around a third.
President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030.
But the project risks friction with Western allies hoping to keep Russia isolated during its war in Ukraine. The route runs along Russia's Arctic coast, and Seoul consulted with Moscow about the journey, including whether the ship needed help to tackle any problems, such as getting stuck in ice.
On its outbound voyage, the vessel passed through Arctic waters and reached its first European port, Felixstowe in Britain, before calling at Rotterdam and Gdansk and returning home via the Arctic.
The trial voyage also highlighted the challenges ahead. Before the departure, PanStar told Reuters it was seeking about 1,300 twenty-foot equivalent units of cargo, but the ship left with 737 TEU of cargo plus empty containers.
Industry experts have said the route's value will depend on reliable schedules, the costs of slowing to avoid ice, special insurance premiums and extra fuel use.

items.title: Middle East war, high debt levels to dominate IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok
items.author: Andrea Shalal
items.creator: Andrea Shalal
items.summary: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Bangkok this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest-ever energy supply shock and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.
items.body:
Finance officials from around the world will gather in Bangkok this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest-ever energy supply shock and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already-sluggish global economic growth.
The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and its inflationary impact, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, being held outside of Washington for the first time in three years.
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told Reuters during a tour of the 300,000 square-meter Queen Sirikit National Convention Center on Sunday evening that 18,000 people were registered to attend the meetings, 4,000 more than the last off-site meetings held in Morocco in October 2023.
SEVERAL FINANCE MINISTERS STAYING AWAY Notably absent will be [USN:L1N45V0KM TEXT:"US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent"], who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handles some "domestic engagements," a US official said. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Kevin Warsh will attend and is slated to participate in a public event with Georgieva on October 16.
Several other finance ministers were also staying home due to domestic budget and election duties, but most central bankers would attend, Georgieva said.
Bessent's decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which the U.S. leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine's battle against Russia's invasion and the U.S. move to impose sanctions on the [USN:L8N45U28I TEXT:"International Criminal Court"].
World Bank President Ajay Banga told Reuters that while global growth had held up better than feared when Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, shutting off some 20% of the world's oil, pressures were building again. Soaring prices for diesel, rising fertilizer prices and a looming [USN:L6N44V0FF TEXT:""super" El Niño weather effect"] that experts say could lead to 450,000 heat-related deaths are all hitting at once.
RELEASE OF RESERVES Group of Seven countries have agreed to [USN:B5N44301Y TEXT:"release 100 million barrels of diesel"] and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower gasoline prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress.
Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"U.S. sanctions"] designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine. The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.
More than 1 billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of the war on February 28, but industry executives say the [USN:L6N45S103 TEXT:"amount of oil in storage"] that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fueling pressure on prices.
Banga said the Bank was not revising down its global forecasts at the moment, but was keeping a close eye on developments. "The real thing is not just El Niño by itself; it's the combination ... What's happening to fertilizer prices? What's happening to energy costs? What's happening to debt? It's that put together that creates its own challenges," he said. "And I think that will call upon all of us to be far more careful on what we prepare for in the coming months."
RISING DEBT IMF chief [USN:L1N45S0Z3 TEXT:"Georgieva"] issued a similar warning in her traditional curtain-raiser speech previewing the meetings last week, telling the audience: "Winter is coming."
The IMF has signaled little change in its forecast for 3% global growth in 2026 and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher. But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia's invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.
IMF research released on Tuesday showed that [USN:L1N45R02Q TEXT:"sharp spikes in food and energy prices"] are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability.
One huge headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures. The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100% of GDP before 2030.
Advanced economies, led by the United States, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, El Niño, and lack of investment in AI, which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries.
EMERGING MARKET CONCERNS Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Together, they face $400 billion in debt payments to external creditors in 2026, and interest payments already exceed 10% of revenue on average.
Early in the COVID crisis, G20 leaders announced a suspension of debt service payments for the poorest countries, but there is little appetite for such action now, according to diplomats from G20 countries, who said high debt levels and political pressures posed bigger hurdles this time.
Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programs that call for fewer, but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures.
"Countries are already cutting their expenditures because their debt payments are going high and because of the IMF conditionality," said Iolanda Fresnillo, who works on debt justice for Eurodad. "We fear that this review of conditionality policy is just going to make things worse."
Kenya, she said, had avoided a debt restructuring by cutting public expenditures and trying to raise taxes, but the changes sparked significant protests, especially by the young.
The IMF risked losing credibility unless it acknowledged the severity of the crisis facing many developing countries.
"As long as they continue with the governance structure that they have, they are becoming less and less relevant," she said.
SECURITY AND FINANCE Flight routes to Bangkok often route through the Middle East, posing immediate security challenges to global travelers descending on Thailand's bustling capital city of 9 million residents following recent [USN:L1N45W03M TEXT:"attacks on Saudi airports"].
The last off-site annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank took place in Morocco just days after militants led by [USN:L8N45S0ZS TEXT:"Hamas killed 1,200 people in Israel"], followed by Israel's bombardment of Gaza that killed more than 74,000 people and devastated cities throughout the Palestinian area.
Three years later, the linkage between national security and international finance is clear, although finance officials at the time had dismissed the Hamas attack as not being an economic issue, said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council.
"Obviously there have been massive global ramifications," he said. "What we're currently experiencing with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has a direct connection with what happened three years ago."
Policymakers needed to become more agile in responding to geopolitical crises in an increasingly interconnected world, Lipsky said. "They have to be proactive and they have to recognize that they don't live in the world they used to."

KATHMANDU: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday (Oct 11) to move to safer places after a massive flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.
A dry landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100km west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said.
The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
"We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.

Mishra said about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges had been swept away, and a hydroelectric project was damaged by the flood.
The flooded river carrying muddy sludge is rising and has washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority.
The army rescued six people from Jagat who were facing the risk of a landslide, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said in a social media post. Another 18 workers at the hydroelectric project that had its camp was damaged escaped to safety, Uprety said.
National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood.
"Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post.
Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

items.title: サッカー＝ロナルドに暫定的な出場停止処分、代表途中離脱で
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１０日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［１０日　ロイター］　 - ポルトガル・サッカー連盟（ＦＰＦ）は１０日、代表合宿中に突如離脱した主将クリスティアノ・ロナルド（４１）に対して懲戒手続きを開始し、暫定的に出場停止処分を科したと発表した。

ロナルドは９月３０日に、欧州ネーションズリーグの試合に向けて遠征中の代表チームから離脱した。その後公開した長文の声明で、コンディション管理のため欠場予定だったノルウェー戦での起用を巡り、ジョルジェ・ジェズス監督は「約束を破った」とコメント。同監督は記者会見で事の経緯を説明すると合意していたものの、実際に話した内容は異なっており、「監督が私との約束を破ったのはこれが２回目だった」と述べていた。

ジェズス監督は、そのような合意はなかったと否定している。

ロナルドは同じ声明の中で合宿地を突然去ったことなどを謝罪し、ＦＰＦの処分を受け入れる意向を示していた。同連盟の規定では、代表チームでの活動を「放棄」した場合は１カ月から６カ月の出場停止処分を科すことになっている。

同選手はすでに所属クラブのアルナスル（サウジアラビア）に戻っており、９日の試合でゴールを決めている。

items.body:
［１０日　ロイター］　 - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は１０日、ア・リーグの地区シリーズ（５回戦制）第５戦を行い、村上宗隆内野手が所属するホワイトソックスはガーディアンズに０─２で敗戦。２連勝の後の３連敗で敗退した。

ホワイトソックスは四回に先発のショーン・バーク投手がガーディアンズの２番ホセ・ラミレス三塁手に先制２ランを打たれ、これが決勝打となった。村上は「４番・一塁」で出場し、４打数ノーヒット、４三振だった。

ガーディアンズの先発ギャビン・ウィリアムズ投手が５回２／３、１安打無失点、１２奪三振の好投で勝利投手となった。同投手は２日前に行われた第４戦では九回途中からリリーフ登板。１８球を投げてチームの勝利に貢献していた。

ＭＬＢ公式サイトによると、ポストシーズンの５回戦制のシリーズで２連敗の後、３連勝したのは２０１７年のヤンキース以来で、メジャー史上１１チーム目。

ガーディアンズは１２日から始まるア・リーグ優勝決定シリーズ（７回戦制）でレイズと対戦する。その前日に開幕するナ・リーグの同シリーズでは大谷翔平選手、山本由伸投手、佐々木朗希投手が所属するドジャースがブルワーズと戦う。

items.title: Nepal urges villagers to evacuate after flood triggered by landslide, 5 missing
items.author: Gopal Sharma
items.creator: Gopal Sharma
items.summary: Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.
items.body:
Nepali authorities urged villagers on Sunday to move to safer places after a flood in a river in the central part of the country swept away several houses and infrastructure, but there were no reports of any casualties.
Two women and three men were out of contact, the national disaster authority said. The army said a further 49 people, including a foreigner, had been rescued. They did not give the person's nationality.
A landslide in Chumnubri village in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding, authorities said.
The Budhi Gandaki is a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
"We have asked villagers living along the river banks downstream to evacuate and remain safe," said Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, the Gorkha district's most senior bureaucrat.
The flood swept away about a dozen houses and two suspension bridges and damaged a hydroelectric project camp, carrying some of the construction equipment away, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said.
The flooded river carrying muddy sludge was rising and had washed away a highway bridge connecting Gorkha with the neighbouring Dhading district, said Dharam Raj Uprety, chief of the Authority.
National disaster authorities alerted people living along the river in the Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, East Nawalparasi and West Nawalparasi districts about the flood.
"Please help ensure that people in at-risk areas are moved to safe locations in time and assist search and rescue operations as needed," the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said in a social media post.
Officials said army and police rescue personnel had reached the area and were also monitoring the situation from a helicopter.

items.title: 韓国コンテナ船、北極海航路で初の欧州往復　定期運航へ課題も
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Joyce Lee

[ソウル １１日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Joyce Lee

[ソウル １１日 ロイター] - 韓国のコンテナ船が１１日、北極海航路で欧州を往復する同国初の商業航海を終え、南東部の釜山港に帰港した。韓国政府は北極海航路の活用を進め、釜山を世界的な海運拠点に育てたい考え。

コンテナ船「パンスタ・アクロ」は８月２２日に釜山を出港し、５０日ぶりに帰港した。韓国当局によると、北極海航路なら通常のルートに比べて航海日数を約３分の１短縮できる可能性がある。李在明大統領は北極海航路の開拓を重点政策に位置付けており、政府は２０３０年までの定期運航開始を目指している。

ただ、航路はロシアの北極圏沿岸を通るため、ウクライナでの戦争を巡りロシアの孤立化を図る西側諸国との摩擦につながる可能性もある。韓国は今回の航海に先立ち、船が氷に閉じ込められた場合などの支援についてロシア側と協議した。

パンスタ・アクロは往路で北極海を通過し、欧州で最初の寄港地となる英国のフェリックストーに到着。その後、ロッテルダムとグダニスクに寄港し、再び北極海を通って帰国した。

今回の航海は商業化に向けた課題も浮き彫りになった。運航会社は出港前、約１３００ＴＥＵ（２０フィート換算のコンテナ数）の貨物確保を目指しているとロイターに説明していたが、実際に積載した貨物は７３７ＴＥＵにとどまった。

items.title: WHO unsure what caused pneumonia that killed plague-lab worker in Russia
items.author: CNA
items.summary: The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media.

WHO unsure what caused pneumonia that killed plague-lab worker in Russia

The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media.

A satellite image shows the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk, Russia, May 8, 2025. (Photo: Reuters via Handout Google/Airbus)

GENEVA: The World Health Organization (WHO) said on Saturday (Oct 10) that it still does not know what caused the pneumonia that killed a Russian lab worker at an anti-plague research centre in Siberia this month, and that no case of plague had been registered.
The WHO said the Russian state regulator reported that tests of the lab worker and those who came in contact with her were negative for the high-threat pathogens tested, that her contacts still showed no symptoms, and that no further linked cases of severe pneumonia had been identified.
"Based on the information provided ... (the) WHO has not identified evidence of ongoing transmission associated with this event. A key uncertainty remains the absence of a confirmed diagnosis in the deceased laboratory worker," it said in a statement.
The lab worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances on Oct 2, prompting authorities to quarantine about 200 people and causing public health fears on social media.
Global health officials have been extra alert to fatal pneumonia cases of undetermined cause since the COVID-19 pandemic, which began with a cluster of fast-spreading fatal respiratory illness in China. The cause of individual pneumonia cases can often not be determined.
Russian authorities have said the lab worker was appropriately vaccinated and that they found no microorganisms linked to her work in her body.
On Thursday, Russia said it had completed health checks on all the worker's contacts. It says it had provided full information to the WHO according to established procedures.

Related:

Commentary: What’s in the melting Russian permafrost may be scarier than plague

items.title: トランプ氏、ウクライナ大統領の交代求める　軽油高騰でロシア製油所攻撃を批判
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Max Hunder　Steve Holland

[１０日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Max Hunder　Steve Holland

[１０日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は１０日、「ウクライナは新しい大統領を選ぶときだと思う」と述べ、ゼレンスキー大統領の交代を求めた。ウクライナによるロシアの製油所への攻撃が世界の軽油供給に打撃を与えていると批判した。

トランプ氏は前日、ロシアから軽油を輸入することで合意したと発表。ゼレンスキー氏は、合意がロシアを勢いづかせたと強く反発した。

米国とイスラエルが２月にイランを攻撃して以降、世界的に軽油価格が急騰しており、来月の米中間選挙を控えてトランプ氏の共和党にとって政治的な重荷となっている。選挙では野党・民主党が上下両院の一方、または両方で多数派を奪還する可能性がある。

トランプ氏が軽油供給合意を発表したのは、ウクライナと欧州の当局者が９日に米マイアミで米側と戦争終結に向けた共通案を協議している最中だった。ゼレンスキー氏によると、発表はウクライナ側にとって予想外だった。

英国のバーナム首相は１０日、ゼレンスキー氏と電話会談し、対ロシア制裁を強化する考えを伝えた。英首相官邸が明らかにした。両首脳は数日中に直接会談する予定という。

items.title: サッカー＝バルセロナ快勝で開幕からの連勝キープ、レアルは辛勝
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［マドリード　１０日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［マドリード　１０日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのスペイン１部は１０日、各地で試合を行い、昨季王者で首位のバルセロナがヘタフェを３─０で下し、開幕から８連勝とした。

バルセロナは前半２分、アンソニー・ゴードンの放ったシュートが相手選手に当たってコースが変わり、ネットを揺らして先制に成功。同３０分にはこの日が新天地での初先発となったガブリエル・ジェズスが加点し、最後はジュール・クンデのゴールで締めくくった。

レアル・マドリードはビリャレアルに１─０で辛勝。後半１７分に１９歳のヤン・ディオマンデがオフサイドトラップをかいくぐって挙げたゴールが決勝点となった。今夏に加入した同選手にとって、これがレアルでの初ゴール。

レアルはその８分後、ビニシウス・ジュニオールがネットを揺らすも、ビデオ・アシスタント・レフェリー（ＶＡＲ）の介入により、ゴール前に相手選手の髪を引っ張っていたとしてノーゴール判定に。さらにジュニオールは一発退場となった。

その他、アトレチコ・マドリードはアラベスに２─１で勝利。ラヨ・バリェカノ─ビルバオの一戦は、スタジアムでラヨのファンがクラブオーナーへの抗議としてピッチに物を投げ込むなどし、１５分間の中断の後に中止となった。

items.title: 米司法省、独禁法違反の疑いでテレビ5社調査　ホワイトハウス取材停止巡り
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター

items.title: テニス＝マスターズ上海大会、第2シードのアルカラス3回戦進出
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１０日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１０日　ロイター］ - テニスのマスターズ上海大会は１０日、男子シングルス２回戦を行い、第２シードのカルロス・アルカラス（スペイン）が３回戦に進んだ。

アルカラスはフアンマヌエル・セルンドロ（アルゼンチン）に６─３、６─３で快勝。８本のサービスエースを放ち、ブレークポイントは１回も握られなかった。ウィナーの本数でも２４─８と上回り、わずか６７分で勝利を収めた。

スペイン人男子による同大会初優勝を目指すアルカラスは、次戦でジズー・ベルグス（ベルギー）と対戦する。ベルグスは２回戦で第３２シードのイグナシオ・ブセ（ペルー）を６─０、６─３で下した。

第４シードのフェリックス・オジェアリアシム（カナダ）、ロシア出身で第５シードのダニル・メドベージェフはともにフルセットで勝ち上がり。第８シードのアルトゥール・フィス（フランス）、第１１シードのテーラー・フリッツ（米国）らも勝ち上がった。

items.title: Ｆ１＝シンガポールＧＰ予選、フェルスタッペンがＰＰ獲得
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［シンガポール　１０日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［シンガポール　１０日　ロイター］　 - 自動車レースＦ１の第１７戦、シンガポール・グランプリ（ＧＰ）は１０日、予選を行い、マックス・フェルスタッペン（オランダ、レッドブル）が２戦連続、キャリア通算５０回目のポールポジション（ＰＰ）を獲得した。

４回の個人総合優勝を誇るフェルスタッペンにとって、今回がＦ１での通算２５０戦目。シャルル・ルクレール（モナコ）が２番手、ルイス・ハミルトン（英国）が３番手とフェラーリ勢が続き、総合首位のキミ・アントネッリ（イタリア、メルセデス）が４番手だった。

昨季の総合王者ランド・ノリス（英国、マクラーレン）は５番手。総合２位のジョージ・ラッセル（英国、メルセデス）は６番手だったが、エンジンのペナルティーにより、決勝では最後尾からのスタートとなる。ノリスの同僚、オスカー・ピアストリ（オーストラリア）は７番手のタイムを計測した。

予選の前に行われたスプリントではフェルスタッペンが勝利。ハミルトンが２位、ルクレールが３位、アントネッリが４位だった。ノリスとピアストリが接触したが、ともにペナルティーは受けなかった。

items.title: 成長の好循環「少しずつ見えてきた」、定着へ責任ある積極財政＝官房長官
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［東京　１１日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［東京　１１日　ロイター］ - 木原稔官房長官は１１日のＮＨＫの報道番組に出演し、高市早苗政権の経済政策により成長の好循環が少しずつ見えてきたと指摘し、変化の兆しが定着するまで「しっかりと責任ある積極財政」を行う考えを示した。

木原氏は、設備投資や雇用の増加が賃金上昇につながり、消費の増加、企業の事業収益、税収増などにつながる成長の好循環が少しずつ見えてきたと分析した。責任ある積極財政により、国内投資を引き出し、潜在成長率を引き上げ、「ＧＤＰが拡大していく中で成長の好循環を実現していきたい」と語った。

物価高対策に関連して補正予算を編成する可能性を問われると、「エネルギー価格の変動にこれから注目していきたい」とした上で、ガソリン価格を１リットル当たり１７０円に抑えている現状を改めて説明。「これに加えて何をしていくかということは、しっかりと影響を注視していきたい」と話した。

items.title: サッカー＝田中先発のリーズ、昨季王者アーセナルに逆転負け
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ロンドン　１０日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［ロンドン　１０日　ロイター］　 - サッカーのイングランド・プレミアリーグは１０日、各地で試合を行い、田中碧が所属するリーズは昨季王者アーセナルに１─２の逆転負けを喫した。

リーズは後半１０分にジェームズ・ジャスティンのゴールで先制したが、その７分後にアーセナルのリッカルド・カラフィオーリに同点ゴールを献上。さらに同２５分、途中出場のブルーノ・ギマランイスにゴール隅へのシュートを決められた。田中は先発し、後半２６分までプレーした。

ＧＫ鈴木彩艶がフル出場したアストンビラはブレントフォードと２─２のドロー。前田大然が所属するイプスウィッチはフラムに２─１で逆転勝ち。前田は先発し、後半３６分までピッチに立った。三笘薫が所属するブライトンはサンダーランドに２─０で勝利。三笘はベンチ入りしなかった。

この他、チェルシーはボーンマスに５─１で圧勝。マンチェスター・ユナイテッドはトットナムと１─１で引き分けた。

６試合を消化したアーセナルが首位マンチェスター・シティー（マンＣ）と同じ勝ち点１５に伸ばし、２位に浮上した。ブライトンが同１３で３位。マンＣは１１日、敵地でリバプールと対戦する。
